title.en: Volume 417 Biographies 176: Qiao Xingjian, Fan Zhong, You Si, Zhao Kui, Xie Fangshu
title.raw: 卷四百十七 列傳第一百七十六 喬行簡 范鍾 游似 趙葵 謝方叔 Volume 417 Biographies 176: Qiao Xingjian, Fan Zhong, You Si, Zhao Kui, Xie Fangshu

sentences.zh: 喬行簡範鍾遊似趙葵

translations.literal: Qiao Xingjian, Fan Zhong, You Si, Zhao Kui
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian, Fan Zhong, You Si, and Zhao Kui

translations.literal: (elder brother Fan) (close annotation bracket)
translations.idiomatic: (elder brother Fan)

sentences.zh: 謝方叔

translations.literal: Xie Fangshu
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangshu

sentences.zh: 喬行簡，字壽朋，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Qiao Xingjian, courtesy name Shoupeng, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian, styled Shoupeng, was from Dongyang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 學於呂祖謙之門。

translations.literal: He studied at the gate of Lü Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 登紹熙四年進士第。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the fourth year of the Shaoxi era (1193).

sentences.zh: 曆官知通州，條上便民事。

translations.literal: In successive offices he served as prefect of Tongzhou and submitted memorials on affairs convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts he served as prefect of Tongzhou, where he submitted memorials outlining measures to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 主管戶部 架閣，召試館職，為秘書省正字兼樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Ministry of Revenue archive; was summoned to an examination for a drafting post and became rectifier of the Secretariat and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Ministry of Revenue archives, was summoned for the drafting examination, and was appointed Secretariat rectifier and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 升秘書郎，為淮西轉運判官，知嘉興府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretary gentleman, served as transport intendant of Huaixi, and was prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to secretary gentleman, he served as Huaixi transport intendant and as prefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 改淮南轉運判官兼淮西提點刑獄、提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport intendant of Huainan, concurrently serving as judicial commissioner of Huaixi and grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Huainan transport intendant, concurrently serving as Huaixi judicial commissioner and grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 言金有必亡之形，中國宜靜 以觀變。

translations.literal: He said that Jin showed the signs of certain destruction, and that China should remain quiet to observe the changes.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Jin state showed clear signs of impending collapse, and that the Song should hold still and watch how events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 因列上備邊四事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed and submitted four matters for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to submit a four-point plan for border defense.

sentences.zh: 會近臣有主戰者，師遂出，金人因破蘄、黃。

translations.literal: It happened that among close ministers there were advocates of war; the army was then sent out, and the Jin people consequently broke Qi and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Just then certain close ministers were urging war; troops were dispatched, and the Jin seized Qi and Huang prefectures in response.

sentences.zh: 移浙西提點刑獄兼知鎮江府。

translations.literal: He was moved to judicial commissioner of Zhexi, concurrently serving as prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zhexi judicial commissioner and concurrent prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎兼國子司業，兼國史編修、實錄檢討，兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to diarist of attendance, concurrently serving as vice-director of the Directorate of Education, compiler of the national history and examiner of the veritable records, and lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to diarist-in-attendance, concurrently serving as vice-director of the Directorate of Education, national history compiler and veritable records examiner, and lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋遷 宗正少卿、秘書監，權工部侍郎，皆任兼職。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice-director of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and supervisor of the Secretariat, and acting vice-minister of Works—all appointments held concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice-director of the Imperial Clan Directorate and supervisor of the Secretariat, with acting appointment as vice-minister of Works, all held concurrently.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，行簡貽書丞相史彌遠，請帝法孝宗行三年喪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, Xingjian sent a letter to Chancellor Shi Miyuan requesting that the Emperor follow Xiaozong's example in observing three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, Xingjian wrote to Chancellor Shi Miyuan urging the emperor to follow Emperor Xiaozong's precedent of observing three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 應詔上疏曰：

translations.literal: In response to an edict he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial edict he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 求賢、求言二詔之 頒，果能確守初意，深求實益，則人才振而治本立，國威張而奸宄銷。

translations.literal: The promulgation of the two edicts seeking worthies and seeking remonstrance—if Your Majesty can truly hold fast to the original intent and deeply seek real benefit, then talent will be invigorated and the foundation of governance established, national prestige will expand and treacherous evildoers will be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can truly hold to the original intent of the two edicts calling for worthies and for candid counsel, and earnestly pursue their practical benefit, then talent will flourish and the foundations of governance will be secured, national prestige will rise, and treachery will be rooted out.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀近事，似或不然。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed recent affairs, and it seems perhaps not so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent affairs, I have observed what seems to be otherwise.

sentences.zh: 夫自侍從至郎官凡幾人，自監司至郡守凡幾人，今其所舉賢能才識之 士又不知其幾人也，陛下蓋嚐摭其一二欲召用之矣。

translations.literal: From attendant ministers down to bureau officials, how many are there in all? From surveillance commissioners down to prefects, how many are there in all? Of the worthy, capable, and talented men they have recommended, one does not know how many there are either; Your Majesty has surely picked out one or two intending to summon and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: From attendant ministers down to bureau officials, how many are there? From surveillance commissioners down to prefects, how many again? Of the worthy and capable men they have recommended, who can say how many? Your Majesty has surely singled out one or two for summons and appointment.

sentences.zh: 凡內外小大之臣囊封來上，或直或巽，或切或泛，無所不有，陛下亦嚐摭其一二見之施行且褒賞之矣。

translations.literal: Of memorials sealed and submitted by inner and outer officials great and small, some are direct and some indirect, some urgent and some general—there is nothing lacking; Your Majesty has also surely picked out one or two, seen them implemented, and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials sealed and submitted by officials within and without the court, great and small, have been forthright or oblique, pointed or broad in every variety; Your Majesty has surely selected one or two for implementation and reward.

sentences.zh: 而天下終 疑陛下之為具文。

translations.literal: Yet the realm in the end suspects that Your Majesty's actions are empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm still suspects that Your Majesty's actions are mere formality.

sentences.zh: 蓋以所召者，非久無宦情決不肯來之人，則年已衰暮決不可來之人耳。

translations.literal: This is because those summoned are either men long without official ambition who are resolved not to come, or men already aged and declining who are certainly unable to come.
translations.idiomatic: For those summoned are either men who have long been free of official ambition and are resolved never to serve, or men already in the decline of age who cannot possibly come.

sentences.zh: 彼風節素著、持正不阿、廉介有守、臨事不撓者，論薦雖多， 固未嚐收拾而召之也。

translations.literal: Those whose integrity is renowned, who hold to the upright and do not flatter, who are incorruptible and principled, and who do not bend before affairs—though recommended in many memorials, they have never been gathered up and summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Men of established integrity, unyielding rectitude, incorruptible principle, and steadfast resolve in office have been recommended again and again, yet never gathered in and summoned.

sentences.zh: 其所施行褒賞者，往往皆末節細故，無關於理亂，粗述古今，不至於抵觸，然後取之以示吾有聽受之意。

translations.literal: What is implemented and rewarded is often mere minor detail, unrelated to order and disorder; it roughly recounts ancient and modern matters without giving offense, and is then taken to show that we have a mind to listen and accept.
translations.idiomatic: What is implemented and rewarded is often trivial detail, bearing no relation to order or chaos—rough sketches of ancient and modern affairs, carefully inoffensive, chosen only to show a willingness to listen.

sentences.zh: 其間亦豈無深憂遠識高出眾見之表， 忠言至計有補聖聽之聰者，固未聞采納而用之也。

translations.literal: Among them, are there not also deep concerns and far-reaching judgments rising above the common view, loyal words and supreme plans that would sharpen the sage ear? Yet one has never heard of their being adopted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Surely among them are far-sighted judgments surpassing common opinion, and loyal counsel that would sharpen the imperial ear—yet none of these has been adopted and put to use.

sentences.zh: 自陛下臨禦至今，班行之彥，麾節之臣，有因論列而去，有因自請而歸。

translations.literal: From the time Your Majesty began to rule until now, among the eminent of the court ranks and the commanders with banners and seals, some have departed because of remonstrance, and some have returned because they requested it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty began to rule, eminent court officials and frontier commanders have left office after remonstrating, or returned home at their own request.

sentences.zh: 其人或以職業有聞，或以言 語自見，天下未知其得罪之由，徒見其置散投閑，倏來驟去，甚至廢罷而鐫褫，削奪而流竄，皆以為陛下黜遠善士，厭惡直言。

translations.literal: Some were known for professional accomplishment, some made themselves seen through words; the realm does not know the reason for their offense, but only sees them assigned to idle posts, coming and going abruptly, even to the point of dismissal and degradation, confiscation and exile—all believing that Your Majesty has removed good men and grown weary of straight speech.
translations.idiomatic: Some were known for their competence, others for outspoken counsel; the realm knows not why they fell from favor, but sees them cast into idle posts, coming and going in sudden turns, even dismissed, degraded, stripped of rank, or exiled—all taking it as proof that Your Majesty rejects good men and despises frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 去者遂以此而得名，朝廷乃因是而致 謗，其亦何便於此。

translations.literal: Those who leave thereby gain a name for it, and the court thereby incurs slander—what convenience is there in this?
translations.idiomatic: Those who leave gain repute for their integrity, while the court reaps slander in consequence—what advantage lies in this?

sentences.zh: 夫賢路當廣而不當狹，言路當開而不當塞，治亂安危，莫不由此。

translations.literal: The path for worthies ought to be broad and not narrow; the path for remonstrance ought to be open and not blocked—order, disorder, safety, and peril all depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: The path for worthies should be wide, not narrow; the path for remonstrance should be open, not closed—on this depends whether the state stands in order or chaos, safety or peril.

sentences.zh: 又言：“敬天命，伸士氣。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Revere Heaven's mandate; extend the spirit of the scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Revere Heaven's mandate and uphold the morale of the scholar-official class."

sentences.zh: 時帝移禦清燕殿，行簡奏“願加畏謹”，且言：“群賢方集，願勿因濟王議異同，致有渙散。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) At that time the Emperor moved his residence to the Clear Serenity Hall; Xingjian memorialized, "I wish that greater reverence and caution be added," and also said: "Worthy men are just now assembled; I pray that because of differences over the Prince of Ji, there be no dispersal."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor moved his residence to the Clear Serenity Hall. Xingjian memorialized, "I pray that Your Majesty add to your reverence and caution," and added: "Worthy men are now assembled; I beg that disputes over the Prince of Ji not cause them to scatter."

sentences.zh: 升兼侍讀，兼國子祭酒、吏部侍郎，權禮部尚書。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He was promoted to concurrent lecturer-in-waiting, concurrent director of the Directorate of Education and vice-minister of Personnel, and acting minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent lecturer-in-waiting, director of the Directorate of Education, vice-minister of Personnel, and acting minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 權刑部尚書，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事，進簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Acting minister of Punishments; he was appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and advanced to co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting minister of Punishments, was appointed academician of the Hall of Enlightenment and co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was then promoted to full co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，疏言：

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died, he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 向者，陛下內廷舉動，皆有稟承。

translations.literal: Formerly, Your Majesty's conduct within the inner court all had someone to report to and receive approval from.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, Your Majesty's conduct within the inner court was always subject to oversight and approval.

sentences.zh: 小人縱有蠱惑幹求之心，猶有所忌憚而不敢發，今者，安能保小人之不萌是心？

translations.literal: Even if petty men had hearts of enticement and solicitation, they still had something to fear and dared not act; now, how can one guarantee that petty men will not conceive such a heart?
translations.idiomatic: Even petty men bent on manipulation and solicitation still had reason to fear and dared not act; now, who can guarantee that such men will not take heart?

sentences.zh: 陛下又安能保聖心之不無少肆？

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty guarantee that in the sage heart there will be not the slightest loosening?
translations.idiomatic: And how can Your Majesty guarantee that the imperial mind will not slacken even slightly?

sentences.zh: 陛下為天下君，當懋建皇極，一循大公，不應私徇小人為其所誤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sovereign of the realm; you ought vigorously to establish the supreme standard, follow the great public good throughout, and not privately favor petty men and be misled by them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sovereign of the realm; you should vigorously uphold the supreme standard, adhere always to the public good, and not privately indulge petty men and be led astray by them.

sentences.zh: 凡為此者，皆戚畹肺肝之親，近習貴幸之臣，奔走使令之輩。

translations.literal: All who do this are relatives by marriage sharing liver and lungs, close attendants of honored favor, and the crowd that runs errands at command.
translations.idiomatic: All who do this are consort kin of the closest ties, favored intimates of the inner court, and the runners who carry out their orders.

sentences.zh: 外取貨財，內壞綱紀。

translations.literal: Outwardly they take goods and wealth; inwardly they destroy statutes and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they seize wealth; inwardly they corrode law and discipline.

sentences.zh: 上以罔人君之聰明，來天下之怨謗；

translations.literal: Above, they obscure the sovereign's clarity and bring the realm's resentment and slander;
translations.idiomatic: Above, they cloud the sovereign's judgment and draw the realm's resentment and reproach;

sentences.zh: 下以撓官府之公道，亂民間之曲直。

translations.literal: Below, they disturb the public justice of officialdom and confuse right and wrong among the people.
translations.idiomatic: below, they subvert official justice and confound right and wrong among the people.

sentences.zh: 縱而 不已，其勢必至於假采聽之言而傷動善類，設眾人之譽而進拔憸人，借納忠效勤之意而售其陰險巧佞之奸。

translations.literal: If indulged without end, the situation will necessarily reach the point of borrowing words of listening and acceptance to harm and move good men, setting up the praise of the multitude to advance and promote crafty men, and borrowing the intent of offering loyalty and diligent service to sell their sinister, crafty, and sycophantic treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Left unchecked, they will inevitably borrow the language of loyal counsel to strike at good men, manufacture popular praise to advance the cunning, and cloak treacherous designs in the guise of devoted service.

sentences.zh: 日積月累，氣勢益張，人主之威權，將為所竊弄而不自知 矣。

translations.literal: Day by day and month by month accumulating, their momentum grows ever greater; the sovereign's authority and power will be stolen and manipulated by them without his knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: Month upon month their power grows; the sovereign's authority will be usurped and manipulated before he even knows it.

sentences.zh: 陛下衰絰在身，愈當警戒，宮庭之間既無所嚴憚，嬪禦之人又視昔眾多，以春秋方富之年，居聲色易縱之地，萬一於此不能自製，必於盛德大有虧損。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wears mourning garments on your person; you ought all the more to be on guard. Within the palace there is now nothing to be strictly feared; the consorts and attendants are also more numerous than before. In the prime of youth, dwelling in a place where sensual pleasure easily leads to indulgence—if at this point you cannot restrain yourself, your great virtue will surely suffer great loss.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still in mourning; you should be all the more vigilant. Within the palace there is no longer anyone to inspire strict restraint, and the number of consorts and attendants has grown. In the prime of youth, dwelling where sensual temptation easily leads to excess—if Your Majesty cannot restrain yourself now, your great virtue will suffer grave harm.

sentences.zh: 願陛下常加警省。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty constantly add vigilance and reflection.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty remain ever vigilant and self-reflective.

sentences.zh: 又論火災求言，乞取其切者付外行之。

translations.literal: He also discussed seeking remonstrance because of the fire disaster, begging that the most urgent be taken and sent outside for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the call for remonstrance after the fire, asking that the most pointed memorials be sent out for implementation.

sentences.zh: 又論許國不當換文資，其當慮者有五；

translations.literal: He also discussed that Xu Guo ought not be transferred to a civil rank; there are five matters that ought to be considered;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Xu Guo should not be transferred to a civil appointment, citing five grounds for concern;

sentences.zh: 鄭損不當帥蜀。

translations.literal: Zheng Sun ought not command Shu.
translations.idiomatic: and that Zheng Sun was unfit to command Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 又言：“時青者，以官則國家之節度，以人則邊陲之大將，一旦遽為李全所戕，是必疑其終為我用，慮變生肘腋，故先其未發驅除之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Shi Qing—in office he is the state's military commissioner, as a man he is a great general of the frontier; suddenly he was slain by Li Quan. This must be because Li Quan doubted that Qing would in the end serve us, feared trouble arising at his elbow, and therefore removed him before it erupted.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Shi Qing was by rank a state commissioner and by stature a frontier commander; yet he was suddenly murdered by Li Quan. Li Quan must have doubted that Qing would remain loyal, feared trouble at his side, and therefore struck before rebellion could break out.

sentences.zh: 竊意軍中必有憤激思奮之 人，莫若乘勢就淮陰一軍拔其尤者以護其師，然後明指殺青者之姓名，俾之誅戮，加贈恤之典於青，則其勢自分，而吾得籍此以製之，則可折其奸心而存吾之大體。

translations.literal: Your servant privately thinks that in the army there must be men indignant and eager to fight; it would be better to seize the momentum, take the Huaiyin army, select the foremost among them to protect their commander, then clearly point out the names of those who killed Qing and have them executed, and add posthumous honors for Qing—then their factions will divide of themselves, and we can thereby control them, break their treacherous hearts, and preserve our great principle.
translations.idiomatic: I believe there are men in the ranks burning with indignation; better to seize the moment, take the Huaiyin army, promote its best to lead the rest, publicly name Qing's killers for execution, and grant Qing posthumous honors—then their factions will split, and we can use that leverage to break their treachery while preserving the larger principle.

sentences.zh: 不然，跋扈者專殺而不敢誅，有功者見殺而不敢訴，彼知朝廷一用柔道而威斷不施，烏保其不遞相視效？

translations.literal: Otherwise, the overbearing will kill with impunity and none will dare execute them; those with merit will see others slain and none will dare appeal. When they know the court uses only the gentle Way and does not apply stern decisiveness, how can one guarantee they will not imitate one another in turn?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the overbearing will kill at will while none dares punish them; men of merit will see comrades slain and none will dare protest. Once they know the court relies on conciliation alone and never acts with decisive force, who can say they will not follow one another's example?

sentences.zh: 則其所當慮者，不獨李全一人而已。”

translations.literal: Then what ought to be considered is not Li Quan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Then the concern is not Li Quan alone.

sentences.zh: 又言：“山陽民散財殫，非凶賊久安之地，當日夜為鴟張之計。

translations.literal: He also said: "The people of Shanyang are scattered and their wealth exhausted; it is not a place where violent bandits can long remain at peace. They ought day and night to plan for arrogant expansion.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The people of Shanyang are dispersed and their wealth exhausted; it is no place where violent bandits can long remain secure. They must be planning day and night to spread their power.

sentences.zh: 揚州城堅勢壯，足以坐製全淮，此曹未必無窺伺之心，或為所入，則淮東俱非我有，不可不先為之慮也。”

translations.literal: The walls of Yangzhou are strong and its position formidable, sufficient to sit and control the whole Huai region; these fellows cannot be without a mind to spy and wait. If they enter it, then all east of the Huai will no longer be ours—we cannot fail to consider this beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's walls are strong and its position commanding, enough to dominate the entire Huai basin; these men surely harbor designs upon it. If they take the city, all of Huaidong will be lost—we cannot afford to ignore the danger."

sentences.zh: 又請屯駐重兵海道，內為吳、越之捍蔽，外為南北之限製。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He also requested that heavy troops be stationed on the sea route, inwardly shielding Wu and Yue, outwardly forming the barrier between north and south.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that heavy forces be stationed along the sea routes, shielding Wu and Yue within and forming the barrier between north and south without.

sentences.zh: 又論：“李全攻圍泰州，剿除之兵今不可已。

translations.literal: He also discussed: "Li Quan is besieging Taizhou; the troops to exterminate him cannot now be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Li Quan is besieging Taizhou; the campaign to destroy him cannot now be halted.

sentences.zh: 此賊氣貌無以逾人，未必有長算深謀，直剽捍勇決，能長雄於其黨耳，況其守泗之西城則失西城，守下邳則失下邳， 守青社則失青社，既又降北，此特敗軍之將。

translations.literal: This bandit's bearing and appearance do not surpass other men; he necessarily has no long calculation or deep strategy—he is simply fierce, bold, and resolute, able to dominate his faction for long. Moreover, when he held the western wall of Si he lost the western wall; when he held Xiapi he lost Xiapi; when he held Qingshe he lost Qingshe; afterward he again surrendered to the north—he is merely a defeated general.
translations.idiomatic: This bandit is no greater in stature or mien than other men; he lacks long-range strategy and relies only on raw ferocity and daring to dominate his followers. He lost the western wall of Si while holding it, lost Xiapi while holding it, lost Qingshe while holding it, and then surrendered to the north—he is nothing but a defeated commander.

sentences.zh: 十年之內，自白丁至三孤，功薄報豐，反背義忘恩，此天理人情之所共憤，惟決意行之。”

translations.literal: Within ten years, from common soldier to the three solitary ministers, his merit was thin and his reward abundant; he turned his back on righteousness and forgot grace—this is what Heaven's principle and human feeling jointly resent. Only resolve to act.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years he rose from common soldier to one of the three highest ministers, rewarded far beyond his merit; then he betrayed loyalty and forgot past grace—a thing that Heaven and men alike condemn. Only firm resolve will suffice."

sentences.zh: 後皆如行簡所料。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Later events all proceeded as Xingjian had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Events afterward unfolded exactly as Xingjian had predicted.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政 事兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice grand councilor, concurrently serving as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice grand councilor and concurrent director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議收復三京，行簡在告，上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time there was discussion of recovering the Three Capitals; Xingjian was on leave and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated recovering the Three Capitals, Xingjian was on sick leave and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 八陵有可朝之路，中原有可復之機，以大有為之資，當有可為之會，則事之有成，固可坐而策 也。

translations.literal: The eight imperial tombs have a path that can be visited; the Central Plain has an opportunity that can be recovered. With the resources of great enterprise, facing an occasion when action is possible—the matter's success can surely be planned while seated.
translations.idiomatic: The eight imperial tombs lie within reach of pilgrimage; the Central Plain offers a chance for recovery. With the resources of a great undertaking and a moment when action is possible, success can be planned from one's seat.

sentences.zh: 臣不憂出師之無功，而憂事力之不可繼。

translations.literal: Your servant does not worry that sending out the army will be without achievement, but worries that strength and resources cannot be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear that the campaign will fail outright; I fear that our strength cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 有功而至於不可繼，則其憂始深矣。

translations.literal: If there is achievement yet it reaches the point where it cannot be sustained, then the worry begins to deepen.
translations.idiomatic: Initial success that cannot be sustained will bring worry far deeper than failure.

sentences.zh: 夫自古英君，必先治內而後治外。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, enlightened rulers have always first governed within and afterward governed without.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, enlightened rulers have always put internal order first and external conquest second.

sentences.zh: 陛下視今日之內治，其已舉乎，其未舉乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, look at today's internal governance—has it been accomplished, or has it not been accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, consider the state of internal governance today—is it complete, or is it not?

sentences.zh: 向未 攬權之前，其敝凡幾？

translations.literal: Before you personally took power, how many were its abuses?
translations.idiomatic: Before you personally assumed rule, how many abuses were there?

sentences.zh: 今既親政之後，其已更新者凡幾？

translations.literal: Now after you have personally governed, how many have been renewed?
translations.idiomatic: Since you began to govern in person, how much has truly been renewed?

sentences.zh: 欲用君子，則其誌未盡伸；

translations.literal: If you wish to employ gentlemen, then their will has not yet fully been extended;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to employ worthy men, their aims have not yet fully been realized;

sentences.zh: 欲去小人，則其心未盡革。

translations.literal: if you wish to remove petty men, then their hearts have not yet fully been reformed.
translations.idiomatic: if you wish to remove petty men, their hearts have not yet fully been changed.

sentences.zh: 上有厲精更始之意，而士大夫之苟且不務任責者自 若。

translations.literal: Above there is the intent to refine the spirit and make a new beginning, yet among scholar-officials those who are perfunctory and do not take responsibility remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Above, Your Majesty shows the will to renew the state, yet among scholar-officials the perfunctory and irresolute remain as they were.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有禁包苴、戒貪墨之令，而州縣之黷貨不知盈厭者自如。

translations.literal: The court has orders forbidding bribes and warning against corruption, yet among prefectures and counties those who covet goods without knowing satiety remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court has forbidden bribery and warned against corruption, yet prefects and magistrates still grasp for gain without surfeit.

sentences.zh: 欲行楮令，則外郡之新券雖低價而莫售；

translations.literal: If you wish to implement the paper-money order, then in outer prefectures the new notes, though at low price, have no buyer;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to enforce the paper-money decree, new notes in the outer prefectures sell at a discount and still find no takers;

sentences.zh: 欲平物價，則京師之百貨視舊直而不殊。

translations.literal: if you wish to level commodity prices, then in the capital the hundred goods compared with old value are not different.
translations.idiomatic: if you wish to stabilize prices, goods in the capital remain no different from their old levels.

sentences.zh: 紀綱法度，多頹 弛而未張；

translations.literal: Statutes, discipline, law, and measure—many are collapsed and slack and not yet restored;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and discipline are largely collapsed and not yet restored;

sentences.zh: 賞刑號令，皆玩視而不肅。

translations.literal: rewards, punishments, proclamations, and orders—all are treated lightly and not enforced with severity.
translations.idiomatic: rewards, punishments, and orders are treated lightly and not enforced with rigor.

sentences.zh: 此皆陛下國內之臣子，猶令之而未從，作之而不應，乃欲闔辟乾坤，混一區宇，製奸雄而折戎狄，其能盡如吾意乎？

translations.literal: These are all Your Majesty's ministers and subjects within the realm, yet though you command them they do not follow, though you act upon them they do not respond—and you wish to open and close Heaven and Earth, unify the whole region, control treacherous heroes and break the barbarians of the Rong—can this fully accord with our intent?
translations.idiomatic: These are Your Majesty's own ministers and subjects, yet they disobey your commands and ignore your initiatives—and you would open the realm, unify the empire, subdue traitors, and break the northern foe: can this fully accord with your intent?

sentences.zh: 此臣之所 憂者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter of which your servant is worried.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first concern.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，欲用其民者，必先得其心以為根本。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, emperors who wished to use their people must first obtain their hearts and take that as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, rulers who wished to mobilize the people had first to win their hearts and make that the foundation.

sentences.zh: 數十年來，上下皆懷利以相接，而不知有所謂義。

translations.literal: For several decades, above and below all have met one another with profit in mind, and do not know what is called righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: For decades, high and low have dealt with one another solely for profit, heedless of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 民方憾於守令，緩急豈有效死勿去之人；

translations.literal: The people just resent the prefects and magistrates; in urgency or crisis, how can there be men who will die without leaving?
translations.idiomatic: The people resent their magistrates; in crisis, who will die rather than flee?

sentences.zh: 卒不愛其將校，臨陳豈有奮勇直前之士。

translations.literal: Soldiers do not love their commanders; facing battle, how can there be men who advance bravely straight ahead?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers do not love their officers; on the battlefield, who will charge forward with courage?

sentences.zh: 蓄怨含憤，積於平日，見難則避，遇敵則奔，惟利是顧，皇恤其他。

translations.literal: Stored resentment and contained anger, accumulated on ordinary days—seeing difficulty they avoid it, meeting the enemy they flee, looking only to profit, how could they spare a thought for anything else?
translations.idiomatic: Resentment stored up over ordinary days means that when hardship comes men shrink back, and when they meet the enemy they flee, caring for profit alone and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 人心如此，陛下曾未有以轉移固結之，遽欲驅之北鄉， 從事於鋒鏑，忠義之心何由而發？

translations.literal: Human hearts are like this; Your Majesty has never had a means to shift and bind them firmly, yet you hastily wish to drive them northward to engage in spear and blade—how can hearts of loyalty and righteousness thereby be aroused?
translations.idiomatic: Such is the temper of the people; Your Majesty has done nothing to turn and bind their hearts, yet would suddenly drive them north to face sword and spear—how can loyalty and righteousness be awakened?

sentences.zh: 況乎境內之民，困於州縣之貪刻，厄於勢家之兼並，饑寒之氓常欲乘時而報怨，茶鹽之寇常欲伺間而竊發，蕭牆之憂凜未可保。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people within the borders are distressed by the greed and harshness of prefectures and counties, constrained by the encroachment and absorption of powerful families; hungry and cold commoners constantly wish to seize the moment to repay resentment, and salt and tea bandits constantly wish to watch for an interval to steal and rise—alarm within the inner wall is still not to be guaranteed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people within our borders suffer under greedy magistrates and powerful families that swallow their lands; the hungry and cold would seize any chance for revenge, and salt and tea smugglers watch for any opening to rise in rebellion—trouble within the palace walls cannot be ruled out.

sentences.zh: 萬 一兵興於外，綴於強敵而不得休，潢池赤子，復有如江、閩、東浙之事，其將奈何？

translations.literal: In the event that war arises outside and is delayed by a strong enemy without being able to rest, the crimson children of the stagnant pool—again there will be affairs like those of Jiang, Min, and eastern Zhe—what then can be done?
translations.idiomatic: If war abroad bogs down against a strong enemy, the common folk—restive as the 'red children' of old—may again erupt as in Jiang, Min, and eastern Zhe: what then?

sentences.zh: 夫民至愚而不可忽，內郡武備單弱，民之所素易也。

translations.literal: The people are most foolish yet cannot be neglected; the military preparedness of inner prefectures is thin and weak—what the people have always found easy.
translations.idiomatic: The people are easily underestimated, yet must not be neglected; the inner prefectures are thinly defended—something the people have always known.

sentences.zh: 往時江、閩、東浙之寇，皆 藉邊兵以製之。

translations.literal: In former times the bandits of Jiang, Min, and eastern Zhe all relied on frontier troops to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Past rebellions in Jiang, Min, and eastern Zhe were suppressed only with frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 今此曹猶多竄伏山谷，窺伺田裏，彼知朝廷方有事於北方，其勢不能以相及，寧不又動其奸心？

translations.literal: Now these fellows still mostly hide and lurk in mountain valleys, spying on fields and hamlets; they know the court just now has business in the north and its power cannot reach them—will they not again stir their treacherous hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Many of these men still lurk in mountain valleys, watching the countryside; knowing the court is occupied in the north and cannot reach them, will they not again stir up treachery?

sentences.zh: 此臣之所憂者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter of which your servant is worried.
translations.idiomatic: This is my second concern.

sentences.zh: 自古英君，規恢進 取，必須選將練兵，豐財足食，然後舉事。

translations.literal: Since ancient times, enlightened rulers, in planning recovery and advance, must first select generals and train soldiers, enrich wealth and fill granaries, and then undertake the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, rulers planning recovery and conquest have first chosen generals, trained troops, filled treasuries and granaries, and only then acted.

sentences.zh: 今邊麵遼闊，出師非止一途，陛下之將，足當一面者幾人？

translations.literal: Now the frontier face is vast and distant; sending out the army is not limited to one route—of Your Majesty's generals, how many suffice to hold one front?
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is vast; a campaign requires more than one route—how many of Your Majesty's generals can hold a front alone?

sentences.zh: 勇而能鬥者幾人？

translations.literal: How many are brave and able to fight?
translations.idiomatic: How many are brave enough to fight?

sentences.zh: 智而善謀者幾人？

translations.literal: How many are wise and good at planning?
translations.idiomatic: How many are wise and skilled in strategy?

sentences.zh: 非屈指得二三十輩，恐不 足以備驅馳。

translations.literal: Unless on one's fingers one can count twenty or thirty such men, I fear they are not sufficient to be driven on expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you can count twenty or thirty such men on your fingers, I fear there are not enough to command in the field.

sentences.zh: 陛下之兵，能戰者幾萬？

translations.literal: Of Your Majesty's soldiers, how many tens of thousands can fight?
translations.idiomatic: How many of Your Majesty's troops can actually fight?

sentences.zh: 分道而趣京、洛者幾萬？

translations.literal: How many tens of thousands would advance by separate routes toward the Capital and Luoyang?
translations.idiomatic: How many would march by separate routes toward Kaifeng and Luoyang?

sentences.zh: 留屯而守淮、襄者幾萬？

translations.literal: How many tens of thousands would remain garrisoned to guard the Huai and Xiang regions?
translations.idiomatic: How many would stay behind to hold the Huai and Xiang lines?

sentences.zh: 非按籍得二三十萬眾，恐不足以事進取。

translations.literal: Unless one obtains two or three hundred thousand men according to the registers, I fear they will not suffice for an enterprise of advance and recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the registers yield two or three hundred thousand men, I fear there will not be enough for a campaign of conquest.

sentences.zh: 借曰帥臣威望素著，以意氣招徠， 以功賞激勸，推擇行伍即可為將，接納降附即可為兵，臣實未知錢糧之所從出也。

translations.literal: Even granting that the commanding ministers have long-standing prestige, that they recruit by spirit and goodwill and encourage by merit rewards, that men chosen from the ranks may at once serve as generals and surrendered adherents may at once serve as soldiers—your servant truly does not know whence money and grain are to come.
translations.idiomatic: Even if frontier commanders of established renown could rally men by force of will and reward, pluck generals from the ranks and turn surrendering bands into armies at once—I still do not see where the money and grain would come from.

sentences.zh: 興師十萬，日費千金，千里饋糧，士有饑色。

translations.literal: To raise an army of one hundred thousand costs a thousand in gold per day; to supply grain over a thousand li leaves soldiers with hunger in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: An army of one hundred thousand costs a thousand in gold each day; haul grain a thousand li, and even your soldiers wear hunger on their faces.

sentences.zh: 今之饋餉，累日不已，至於累月，累 月不已，至於累歲，不知累幾千金而後可以供其費也。

translations.literal: At present provisions are supplied day after day without end, extending to month after month; month after month without end, extending to year after year—I do not know how many thousands in gold must accumulate before their costs can be met.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies now drain day after day without end, mounting to months and then years—who knows how many thousands in gold must pile up before the expense can be met?

sentences.zh: 今百姓多垂罄之室，州縣多赤立之帑，大軍一動，厥費多端，其將何以給之？

translations.literal: Now many common people have households drained to the last, and many prefectures and counties have treasuries stripped bare; once the great army moves, its costs branch out in many directions—how then will they be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Many households are already emptied to the last coin; many county treasuries stand bare. Once the main army moves, costs multiply on every side—how will they be paid?

sentences.zh: 今陛下不愛金幣以應邊臣之求， 可一而不可再，可再而不可三。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not begrudge gold and coin to answer the requests of frontier ministers—a thing that may be done once but not twice, twice but not thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is spending gold and silver freely to meet frontier commanders' demands—but that can be done once, perhaps twice, not a third time.

sentences.zh: 再三之後，兵事未已，欲中輟則廢前功，欲勉強則無事力。

translations.literal: After the third time the military affair still does not end; if you wish to break off midway, earlier achievements are wasted; if you wish to press on by force, there is no strength or resources.
translations.idiomatic: After the third round, war still drags on; halt midway and earlier gains are lost; press on by force and there is nothing left to sustain it.

sentences.zh: 國既不足，民亦不堪。

translations.literal: The state is already insufficient, and the people can also no longer bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The state is already exhausted, and the people can bear no more.

sentences.zh: 臣恐北方未可圖，而南方已先騷動矣。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the north may not yet be attainable, while the south has already been stirred up first.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the north may prove unattainable while the south erupts first.

sentences.zh: 中原蹂踐之 餘，所在空曠，縱使東南有米可運，然道裏遼遠，寧免乏絕，由淮而進，縱有河渠可通，寧無盜賊邀取之患？

translations.literal: After the trampling of the Central Plain, everywhere is empty and desolate; even if the southeast has rice that can be transported, yet the road is far and distant—how can shortage and cut-off be avoided? Advancing by the Huai, even if canals may be opened, how can one be free of the trouble of bandits intercepting and seizing?
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain, trampled underfoot, lies empty and abandoned. Even if grain can be shipped from the southeast, the distances are vast and shortages inevitable. Advance along the Huai, and even with canals open, bandits will intercept supplies.

sentences.zh: 由襄而進，必須負載二十鍾而致一石，亦恐未必能達。

translations.literal: Advancing by Xiang, one must carry twenty zhong to deliver one shi—I fear it may not even reach its destination.
translations.idiomatic: An advance through Xiang would require twenty zhong hauled for every shi delivered—and even that may never arrive.

sentences.zh: 若頓師千里之外，糧道不繼，當此之時，孫、吳為謀主，韓、彭為兵帥，亦恐無以為策。

translations.literal: If the army halts a thousand li away and the supply route is not maintained, at such a time even with Sun Wu as chief planner and Han Xin and Peng Yue as commanders, I fear there would be no stratagem left.
translations.idiomatic: If the army camps a thousand li away and supply lines fail, not even Sun Wu plotting and Han Xin and Peng Yue leading troops could save the situation.

sentences.zh: 他日運糧不繼，進退不能，必勞聖慮，此臣之所憂者三也。

translations.literal: Another day, when grain transport is not maintained and advance and retreat are both impossible, it will surely burden the sage concern—this is the third matter of which your servant is worried.
translations.idiomatic: When grain runs out and the army can neither advance nor retreat, Your Majesty's mind will be sorely burdened—this is my third concern.

sentences.zh: 願陛下堅持聖 意，定為國論，以絕紛紛之說。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would firmly hold the sage intent, fix the policy of the state, and cut off the many conflicting opinions.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will hold firm to your intent, fix the policy of the state, and silence the clamor of opposing views.

sentences.zh: 不果從。

translations.literal: The advice was not followed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not adopt his advice.

sentences.zh: 進知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He advanced to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to head the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議禦閱不果，反驟汰之，殿司軍哄，為之黜主帥，罷都司官，給黃榜撫存，軍 愈呼噪。

translations.literal: At that time discussion of an imperial review did not materialize; instead troops were suddenly culled. The Palace Guard mutinied; for this the chief commander was dismissed, the metropolitan command staff abolished, and yellow placards issued to soothe and reassure them—yet the army grew only more clamorous.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial troop review fell through and the court abruptly purged the ranks instead, the Palace Guard mutinied. The chief commander was dismissed, the metropolitan staff abolished, and yellow placards posted to reassure the men—but the uproar only grew.

sentences.zh: 行簡以聞，戮為首者二十餘人，眾乃帖息。

translations.literal: Xingjian reported this; more than twenty ringleaders were executed, and the crowd then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian reported the matter; more than twenty ringleaders were executed, and the troops quieted.

sentences.zh: 尋拜右丞相，言“三京撓敗之餘，事與前異，但當益修戰守之備。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed right grand councilor, saying: "After the battering of the Three Capitals, affairs differ from before; one should only further strengthen preparations for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed right grand councilor, saying: "After the shattering of the Three Capitals, affairs differ from before; we should strengthen our defenses for war.

sentences.zh: 襄陽失守，請急收復。”

translations.literal: Xiangyang has fallen—I beg that it be urgently recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang has been lost—it must be recovered at once."

sentences.zh: 或又陳進取之計，行 簡奏：“今內外事勢可憂而不可恃者七。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Some again presented plans for advance and recovery. Xingjian memorialized: "At present, inner and outer affairs present seven matters that may be worried over but cannot be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: Others again urged offensive plans. Xingjian submitted a memorial: "Present conditions at home and abroad offer seven grounds for worry and none for complacency."

sentences.zh: 言甚懇切，師得不出。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) His words were very earnest and urgent, and the army was therefore not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with such urgency that the campaign was not launched.

sentences.zh: 行簡曆練老成，識量弘遠，居官無所不言。

translations.literal: Xingjian was seasoned and mature in experience, broad and far-reaching in judgment and capacity, and in office spoke out on everything.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was seasoned and far-sighted; in office he held back nothing.

sentences.zh: 好薦士，多至顯達，至於舉錢時、吳如愚，又皆當時隱逸之賢者。

translations.literal: He liked to recommend scholars, many of whom rose to eminence; as for recommending Qian Shi and Wu Ruyu, both were reclusive worthies of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to recommend talent, many of whom rose to high office; among them Qian Shi and Wu Ruyu were reclusive worthies of the day.

sentences.zh: 所著有《周禮總說》、《孔山文集》。

translations.literal: His written works include General Exposition of the Rites of Zhou and the Kongshan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include General Exposition of the Rites of Zhou and the Kongshan Collection.

sentences.zh: 範鍾，字仲和，婺州蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhong, courtesy name Zhonghe, was a native of Lanxi in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhong, styled Zhonghe, was from Lanxi in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the second year of the Jiading era (1209).

sentences.zh: 曆官調武學博士，添差通判太平州，知徽州。

translations.literal: In successive offices he was transferred to doctorate of the Military Academy, added-duty vice prefect of Taizhou, and prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts he served as doctorate of the Military Academy, added-duty vice prefect of Taizhou, and prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，遷刑部郎官，又遷尚右郎官兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was transferred to a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, then to a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue concurrently serving as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was made a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, then in the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent appointment as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 進對，帝 曰：“仁宗時甚多事。”

translations.literal: In an audience he responded to the throne; the Emperor said: "In the time of Emperor Renzong there were very many affairs."
translations.idiomatic: At an audience the Emperor said: "In Emperor Renzong's reign there was no end of business."

sentences.zh: 鍾對曰：“仁宗始雖多事，乃以憂勤致治。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Zhong replied: "At the beginning Emperor Renzong had many affairs, yet through anxious diligence he brought about good order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong replied: "Renzong began with much to manage, yet through anxious diligence brought the realm to order.

sentences.zh: 徽宗始雖無事，餘患至於今日。”

translations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Huizong had no affairs, yet the remaining troubles extend to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong began with little to manage, yet the troubles he left reach down to our own day."

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部郎中兼說書，又遷秘書少監、國子司業兼國史 編修、實祿檢討。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel concurrently serving as lecturer, then to vice director of the Secretariat, vice director of the Directorate of Education concurrently serving as compiler of the national history and examiner of the veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel and lecturer, then vice director of the Secretariat and vice director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently compiling the national history and examining the veritable records.

sentences.zh: 拜起居郎兼祭酒，權兵部侍郎兼同修國史、實祿同修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed diarist of attendance concurrently serving as director of the Directorate of Education, acting vice-minister of War concurrently serving as co-compiler of the national history and co-compiler of the veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed diarist of attendance and director of the Directorate of Education, acting vice-minister of War and co-compiler of the national history and veritable records.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎兼給事中，權兵部尚書兼侍講，尋兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice-minister of War concurrently serving as supervising censor, acting minister of War concurrently serving as lecturer-in-waiting, and soon concurrently reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice-minister of War and supervising censor, then acting minister of War and lecturer-in-waiting, soon adding reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞 密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaxi (1239) he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，授參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，乞歸田裏，不許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he begged to return to his home fields; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou (1241) he asked to retire to his home village; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 四年，知樞密院事，乞歸田裏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and begged to return to his home fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and again asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 五年，特拜左丞相兼樞密使，封東陽郡公，再乞歸田裏，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was specially appointed left grand councilor concurrently serving as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang Commandery, and again begged to return to his home fields; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was specially appointed left grand councilor and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Dongyang, and again asked to retire; again the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 六年，復 請，許之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he requested again and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked once more and was permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 加觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，辭不拜，以保晚節，乃提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey concurrently serving as reader-in-waiting; he declined to accept, wishing to preserve his integrity in old age, and therefore became administrator of the Tongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent appointment as reader-in-waiting; he declined, wishing to preserve his reputation in old age, and took appointment as administrator of the Tongxiao Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，薨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, he passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 鍾為相，直清守法，重惜名器，雖無赫赫可稱，而清德雅量，與杜範、李宗勉齊名。

translations.literal: As chief minister, Zhong was upright, pure, and law-abiding, and he valued official titles highly; though he had no great achievements to his name, in pure virtue and generous bearing he ranked with Du Fan and Li Zongmian.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister, Zhong was upright and law-abiding and guarded official titles jealously; though he won no spectacular renown, in pure conduct and generous bearing he stood with Du Fan and Li Zongmian.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，諡文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor with the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《禮記解》。

translations.literal: His written works include Exposition of the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Exposition of the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遊似，字景仁，利路提點刑獄仲鴻之子。

translations.literal: You Si, courtesy name Jingren, was the son of You Zhonghong, judicial commissioner of the Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: You Si, styled Jingren, was the son of You Zhonghong, judicial commissioner of the Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年進士，曆官為大理司直，升大理寺丞，遷太常丞兼權兵部郎官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourteenth year of Jiading, he served in successive offices as direct clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was transferred to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrently serving as acting bureau director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1221, he rose through the Court of Judicial Review to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting bureau director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞兼權考功郎中、直秘閣、夔路轉運判官，移潼川提點刑獄兼提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant director of the Secretariat concurrently serving as acting bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, as a member of the Privy Repository, as transport intendant of the Kuizhou Circuit, and moved to judicial commissioner of the Tongchuan Circuit concurrently serving as grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became assistant director of the Secretariat and acting bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, member of the Privy Repository, Kuizhou transport intendant, then Tongchuan judicial commissioner and grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 請封諡田錫，從之。

translations.literal: He requested posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous title for Tian Xi; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for posthumous honors for Tian Xi; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監、宗正少卿兼權樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Directorate of Armaments and vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan concurrently serving as acting chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Directorate of Armaments and vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, concurrently acting chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時暫兼權禮部侍郎兼侍講、權禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At that time he temporarily held concurrent appointment as acting vice-minister of Rites concurrently serving as lecturer-in-waiting and as acting vice-minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he also held concurrent appointment as acting vice-minister of Rites and lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 有事於明堂，似上疏言：“欲盡事天之禮，當盡敬天之心。

translations.literal: When there was a ceremony at the Bright Hall, Si submitted a memorial, saying: "If one wishes fully to perform the rites of serving Heaven, one must fully devote the heart that reveres Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall rites were performed, Si submitted a memorial: "To fulfill the rites of serving Heaven, one must fully devote the heart that reveres Heaven.

sentences.zh: 心存則政事必適其宜，言動必當其理，雨蛇菴循其序，夷夏必 安其生。”

translations.literal: When the heart is present, governance must fit its proper measure, words and actions must accord with reason, rain and sunshine must follow their proper seasons, and barbarians and Chinese alike must be secure in their lives.
translations.idiomatic: With the heart truly present, governance will be fitting, words and deeds will accord with reason, rain and sunshine will follow their seasons, and both Chinese and barbarians will live in peace."

sentences.zh: 兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，權禮部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Concurrently co-compiler of the national history and co-compiler at the Veritable Records Academy, acting minister of Rites concurrently serving as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently co-compiler of the national history and veritable records, acting minister of Rites and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 言：“軍賞冒濫，請給告之製，奏功者書填真命付之，候從軍十年，別能立功，升至統領已上，方許從 所屬保明申朝廷，立名給告，則冒濫者革，功勞者勸。”

translations.literal: He said: "Military rewards are recklessly dispensed; I request a system of formal patents. Those reporting merit should have the true commission written and filled out and delivered to them; only after ten years in the army, if they separately achieve merit and are promoted to commander or above, should they be permitted to have their immediate superiors certify and report to the court, establish a name, and receive a patent—then the reckless will be eliminated and the meritorious encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Military rewards are dispensed too freely. I propose a patent system: when merit is reported, a written commission should be issued on the spot; only after ten years of service, with further merit and promotion to commander or above, should superiors certify the record to the court and a formal patent be granted—then abuse would cease and merit would be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書兼給事中兼修國史、實錄院修撰，權工部侍郎，充四川宣撫司參讚軍事兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of Rites concurrently serving as supervising censor and compiler of the national history and Veritable Records Academy, acting vice-minister of Works, and staff officer of the Sichuan Pacification Commission concurrently serving as supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of Rites and supervising censor, compiler of the national history and veritable records, acting vice-minister of Works, and staff officer on the Sichuan Pacification Commission with concurrent appointment as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，入侍經幄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of Personnel and attended the classics mat in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of Personnel and attended the classics mat in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 帝問：“唐太宗貞觀治效何速如是？”

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "How could Emperor Taizong of Tang achieve the results of the Zhenguan reign so swiftly?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "How did Emperor Taizong achieve the results of the Zhenguan reign so swiftly?"

sentences.zh: 似對曰：“人主一念之烈，足以旋乾轉坤。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Si replied: "A single fierce thought in the ruler's heart is enough to turn Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Si replied: "A single resolute thought in a ruler's heart can turn Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 或謂霸圖速而王道遲，不知一日歸仁，期月而可，王道曷 嚐不速。

translations.literal: Some say the path of hegemony is swift while the kingly Way is slow, not knowing that in one day one may return to benevolence, and in a full month it can be achieved—how has the kingly Way ever been slow?
translations.idiomatic: Some say hegemony comes quickly while the kingly Way comes slowly; yet benevolence may be restored in a day and established in a month—the kingly Way has never been slow.

sentences.zh: 一念有時間斷，則無以挽回天下之大勢。

translations.literal: If for a time a thought is interrupted, there is no means to turn back the great momentum of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: But let that thought lapse for even a moment, and the great momentum of the realm cannot be recovered.

sentences.zh: 至於憂勤，既切宸念，而佐理非人，亦何以布宣九重之實。”

translations.literal: As for anxious diligence, though it has cut deeply into the imperial mind, if those who assist in governance are not the right men, how can the reality within the Ninefold Palace be proclaimed?
translations.idiomatic: Anxious diligence may fill the imperial mind, yet if the wrong men assist in governance, how can the truth within the palace be made real?"

sentences.zh: 乃摭太宗事以陳，且謂：“太宗矜心易啟，漸弗克 終，僅止貞觀之治。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Thereupon he gathered Taizong's deeds to set them forth, and said: "Taizong's heart of self-congratulation was easily opened; he gradually could not hold to the end, and good order stopped at the Zhenguan reign alone.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited Taizong's example and said: "Taizong's heart was easily opened to self-congratulation; he could not sustain his effort to the end, and good order stopped with the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣服十有五年，艱危之勢滋甚，回視太宗治效敏速、相越乃爾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne for more than fifteen years; perilous conditions grow ever worse. Looking back at Taizong's swift results in governance, the distance between you is just so great.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned more than fifteen years, and peril grows ever worse. Compared with Taizong's swift achievement of good order, the distance is vast.

sentences.zh: 意者親儒而從諫，敬畏以檢身，未若貞觀之超卓乎？

translations.literal: Perhaps in honoring the ru and heeding remonstrance, in reverence and awe to examine the self—you are not as surpassing as in the Zhenguan reign?
translations.idiomatic: In honoring scholars and heeding remonstrance, in reverence and self-discipline—are you as surpassing as in the Zhenguan reign?

sentences.zh: 節用以致愛，選廉以共 理，未若貞觀之切至乎？

translations.literal: In economizing expenditure to extend care, in selecting the incorrupt to govern together—you are not as pressing and thorough as in the Zhenguan reign?
translations.idiomatic: In frugality to extend care to the people, in selecting the incorrupt to govern together—are you as pressing and thorough as in the Zhenguan reign?

sentences.zh: 願陛下益加聖心。”

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would further strengthen the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will strengthen your resolve still further.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年正月，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事，封南充縣伯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiaxi he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Earl of Nanchong County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jiaxi (1239) he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Earl of Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 八月，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he received appointment as vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年閏月，知樞密院 事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the fourth year he became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently serving as vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month of the fourth year he became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀，仍奉朝請，授知樞密院事兼參知政事，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he became administrator of the Wanshou Abbey concurrently serving as reader-in-waiting, still attending court audiences, was appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs concurrently serving as vice grand councilor, and was promoted in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunyou (1244) he became administrator of the Wanshou Abbey and reader-in-waiting, still attending court, then director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor, and was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed right grand councilor concurrently serving as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed right grand councilor and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十上章，乞歸田裏，帝不許。

translations.literal: Ten times he submitted memorials begging to return to his home fields; the Emperor did not grant this.
translations.idiomatic: Ten times he memorialized asking to retire; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，特 授觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使兼侍讀，進爵國公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was specially appointed grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey concurrently serving as reader-in-waiting, and was promoted in rank to state duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was specially appointed grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent appointment as reader-in-waiting, and promoted to state duke.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉兩官致仕，薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced two ranks and retired from office, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was advanced two ranks, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 特贈少師。

translations.literal: He was specially granted posthumous enfeoffment as Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 趙葵，字南仲，京湖製置使方之子。

translations.literal: Zhao Kui, courtesy name Nanzhong, was the son of Zhao Fang, commissioner of the Jinghu Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kui, styled Nanzhong, was the son of Zhao Fang, commissioner of the Jinghu Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 初生時，或夢南嶽神降其 家。

translations.literal: At the time of his birth, someone dreamed that the god of Mount Heng descended upon the household.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth someone dreamed that the god of Mount Heng descended upon the household.

sentences.zh: 方在襄陽，命葵專督飲食共養之事。

translations.literal: When Fang was at Xiangyang, he ordered Kui to oversee exclusively the affairs of food, drink, and common sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang was at Xiangyang, he put Kui in charge of provisions and daily supplies.

sentences.zh: 與兄範俱有誌事功，方器之，聘鄭清之、全子才為之師。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Fan he had the will to achieve merit in affairs; Fang valued them and engaged Zheng Qingzhi and Quan Zicai as their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Fan both burned to achieve something; Fang valued them and engaged Zheng Qingzhi and Quan Zicai as their tutors.

sentences.zh: 又遣從南康李燔為有用之學。

translations.literal: He also sent Kui to follow Li Fan of Nankang to pursue useful learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Kui to study under Li Fan of Nankang, pursuing practical learning.

sentences.zh: 每聞警報，與諸將偕出，遇敵則深入 死戰，諸將惟恐失製置子，盡死救之，屢以此獲捷。

translations.literal: Whenever an alarm was heard, he went out together with the generals; when they met the enemy he plunged deep and fought to the death. The generals all feared losing the pacification commissioner's son and all fought to the death to save him; repeatedly by this means he won victories.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever alarms sounded he rode out with the generals; when they met the enemy he plunged into the thick of battle. The generals, fearing for the pacification commissioner's son, fought desperately to save him—and again and again victory came of it.

sentences.zh: 一日，方賞將士，恩不償勞，軍欲為變。

translations.literal: One day Fang was rewarding the officers and soldiers; the favor did not match their labor, and the army was about to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: One day Fang rewarded his officers, but the gifts did not match their service and the army was on the verge of mutiny.

sentences.zh: 葵時十二三，覺之，亟呼曰：“此朝廷賜也，本司別有賞齎。”

translations.literal: Kui was then twelve or thirteen; he noticed it and urgently cried out: "This is what the court has bestowed; our command has separate rewards besides."
translations.idiomatic: Kui was twelve or thirteen; sensing trouble, he cried out: "This is the court's gift; our command has separate rewards besides."

sentences.zh: 軍心賴 一言而定，人服其機警。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The hearts of the army relied on this one word and were settled; people admired his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: That single sentence steadied the troops; all marveled at his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年，金將高琪、烏古論慶壽犯襄陽，圍棗陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading the Jin generals Heshilie Gui and Wugulun Qingshou invaded Xiangyang and besieged Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiading (1217) the Jin generals Heshilie Gui and Wugulun Qingshou invaded Xiangyang and besieged Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 時邊烽久熄，金兵猝至，人情震懼。

translations.literal: At that time frontier beacons had long been quiet; the Jin army arrived suddenly, and popular feeling was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier had long been quiet; the Jin army came suddenly and the people were stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 方帥範、葵往戰，敗走之。

translations.literal: Fang led Fan and Kui out to battle and routed them in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Fang led Fan and Kui into battle and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 十三年， 方遣葵及都統扈再興攻金人至高頭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Fang dispatched Kui and the commander-in-chief Hu Zaixing to attack the Jin people as far as Gaotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Fang sent Kui and commander-in-chief Hu Zaixing to attack the Jin as far as Gaotou.

sentences.zh: 高頭，金人必守之處也，出勁兵拒戰，葵率先鋒奮擊，再興繼進殲之。

translations.literal: Gaotou was a place the Jin were sure to defend; they sent crack troops to resist in battle. Kui led the vanguard in fierce attack, and Zaixing followed and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotou was a place the Jin were certain to hold; they sent crack troops to resist. Kui led the vanguard in a fierce assault, Zaixing followed, and the enemy was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 翼日，進次鄧州，金人阻沘河以拒。

translations.literal: The next day they advanced and halted at Dengzhou; the Jin people blocked the Bi River to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they advanced to Dengzhou, where the Jin blocked the Bi River to resist.

sentences.zh: 葵麾軍進擊，楊義諸 將繼至，金兵亦大出合戰，大破之，俘斬及降者幾二萬，獲萬戶而下十數人，奪馬八百，逐北直傅城下而還。

translations.literal: Kui commanded the army to advance and attack; the generals Yang Yi and others followed in succession. The Jin army also came out in force for a combined battle and was greatly defeated. Captives killed and those who surrendered numbered nearly twenty thousand; more than ten men of rank from ten-thousand-household commander downward were taken; eight hundred horses were seized; pursuing north they pressed straight to beneath the walls and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kui led the attack; generals including Yang Yi joined the fight. The Jin came out in force; in the general engagement they were routed. Nearly twenty thousand were killed, captured, or surrendered; more than ten officers of ten-thousand-household rank and below were taken, eight hundred horses seized, and the pursuit pressed to the city walls before they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十四年，金人犯蘄州，葵與範攻唐、鄧。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Jin people invaded Qizhou; Kui and Fan attacked Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Jin invaded Qizhou; Kui and Fan attacked Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 方命之曰：“不克敵，毋相見也。”

translations.literal: Fang ordered them, saying: "If you do not defeat the enemy, do not see me again."
translations.idiomatic: Fang gave them their orders: "If you fail to defeat the enemy, do not come back to face me."

sentences.zh: 三月丁亥，至唐州，薄城而陳。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) On the third month, day dinghai, they reached Tangzhou, approached the city, and deployed in formation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day dinghai, they reached Tangzhou, drew up before the walls, and formed battle lines.

sentences.zh: 金大將阿海引兵出戰，葵帥精騎赴敵，再興從之，大捷，斬馘萬餘。

translations.literal: The Jin grand general Ahhai led troops out to battle; Kui commanded elite cavalry to meet the enemy, Zaixing followed him, and they won a great victory, beheading and counting more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin grand general Ahhai led his troops out to fight. Kui took elite cavalry to meet them, Zaixing followed, and they won a great victory, killing more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 金人閉門不出。

translations.literal: The Jin people shut the gates and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin shut the city gates and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 時金人陷蘄 州者至久長，數十騎出山椒，葵帥楊大成以十四騎逐之。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin who had long held Qizhou sent several dozen horsemen down from the mountain paths; Kui led Yang Dacheng with fourteen horsemen in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had held Qizhou for a long time. Several dozen horsemen came down from the hills; Kui led Yang Dacheng and fourteen riders in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 金騎漸益至數百，葵力戰連破之，而金步騎大集。

translations.literal: Jin cavalry gradually increased to several hundred; Kui fought hard and repeatedly broke them, but Jin infantry and cavalry gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Jin horsemen swelled to several hundred. Kui fought hard and broke them again and again, but Jin foot and horse forces were massing in strength.

sentences.zh: 會範、再興軍合戰，至夜分始解。

translations.literal: Fan's and Zaixing's armies joined the battle; only at midnight did the fighting end.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's and Zaixing's forces joined the fight, and battle did not break off until well past nightfall.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，官軍分二陣，範 將左，再興將右，葵帥突騎左右策應。

translations.literal: On day gengyin the government army divided into two formations: Fan commanded the left, Zaixing the right, and Kui led shock cavalry to support both flanks.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengyin the government forces split into two lines—Fan on the left, Zaixing on the right—while Kui led shock cavalry to support both wings.

sentences.zh: 金人背山亦分為二以相當，而不先動。

translations.literal: The Jin, with the mountain at their backs, also divided into two to meet them, but did not move first.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, backed by the mountain, likewise split into two formations to meet them, but held their ground and did not strike first.

sentences.zh: 範曰：“金人必復謀夜戰以幸勝，乃預備大鼓，令軍中聞疊鼓聲始動，若彼未至五十步 內而輒動者斬。

translations.literal: Fan said: "The Jin are sure to plan a night battle again hoping for victory. Therefore prepare large drums and order the army not to move until layered drumbeats are heard; whoever moves before the enemy comes within fifty paces shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "The Jin will surely try a night attack again, hoping for a lucky victory. Prepare large drums and order the men not to move until they hear repeated drum rolls. Anyone who moves before the enemy is within fifty paces will be executed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金兵稍下山，再興遽衝之，果為敵所乘，遂逼範軍。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin army came slightly down the mountain; Zaixing suddenly charged them, was indeed taken advantage of by the enemy, and thus pressed upon Fan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin troops began descending the slope. Zaixing charged prematurely, the enemy turned it against him, and Fan's line was driven back.

sentences.zh: 範疊鼓麾軍突鬥，葵繼進，殲金兵數千。

translations.literal: Fan beat the layered drums and commanded the army in a sudden assault; Kui followed in advance and annihilated several thousand Jin soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fan rolled the drums and led a sudden charge; Kui pressed forward after him and cut down several thousand Jin troops.

sentences.zh: 敵並力向再興，葵率土豪祝文蔚等以精騎橫衝 之，金人僵屍相屬。

translations.literal: The enemy combined their strength against Zaixing; Kui led the local strongmen Zhu Wenwei and others with elite cavalry in a lateral charge, and Jin corpses lay one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy concentrated against Zaixing. Kui led local leaders including Zhu Wenwei with elite cavalry in a flanking charge, and Jin dead piled up in unbroken rows.

sentences.zh: 復相持至夜分，金人雖斂，而陣如故。

translations.literal: They again held each other until midnight; although the Jin withdrew somewhat, their formation remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides locked in stalemate again until deep night. The Jin pulled back slightly, but their formation held firm.

sentences.zh: 範、葵急會將校，選死士數千，黎明四面奮擊，喚聲撼山谷。

translations.literal: Fan and Kui urgently gathered the officers, selected several thousand death-defying warriors, and at dawn struck fiercely on all four sides; their battle cries shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Kui hastily assembled their officers, picked several thousand shock troops, and at dawn attacked on every side; their war cries shook the valleys.

sentences.zh: 金人走，乘勝逐北，斬首數千級，副統軍投 戈降，拔所掠子女萬餘，得輜重器械山積。
