translations.literal: The Jin fled; pursuing the victory northward they beheaded several thousand; the deputy commander-in-chief cast aside his weapons and surrendered; they recovered more than ten thousand men and women who had been seized, and obtained baggage trains and weapons piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin broke and ran. Pressing the pursuit, they took several thousand heads. The deputy commander threw down his weapons and surrendered. More than ten thousand captives were freed, and wagons, gear, and weapons were captured in mountainous heaps.

sentences.zh: 補葵承務郎、知棗陽軍，範授安撫司內機。

translations.literal: Kui was appointed registrar and military prefect of Zaoyang; Fan was granted the post of internal officer of the pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was appointed registrar and prefect of Zaoyang garrison; Fan was made internal officer of the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 方卒，十五年，起復直秘閣、通判廬州，進大理司直、淮西安撫 參議官。

translations.literal: When Fang died, in the fifteenth year Kui was recalled from mourning as direct attache of the Secret Pavilion and administrative vice-prefect of Luzhou, and was advanced to rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review and planning officer of the Huai West Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Fang died, in the fifteenth year Kui returned from mourning as direct attache of the Secret Pavilion and vice-prefect of Luzhou, then was promoted to rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review and planning officer on the Huai West Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 十七年，李全往青州，淮東製置使許國檄葵議兵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Li Quan went to Qingzhou; Xu Guo, commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission, issued an order summoning Kui to discuss troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Li Quan went to Qingzhou. Xu Guo, commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission, summoned Kui to consult on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 葵至曰：“君侯欲圖賊，而坐賊阱中，悔已無及，惟有重帳前兵，猶足製之爾。”

translations.literal: When Kui arrived he said: "My lord wishes to deal with the bandits, yet sits in their trap; regret is already too late. Only by strengthening the troops before your tent can you still control them."
translations.idiomatic: When Kui arrived he said: "You mean to destroy the rebels, yet you sit in their trap. Regret will come too late. Strengthen the troops at your headquarters, and you can still keep them in check."

sentences.zh: 國曰：“兵不能集，集 不能精，奈何？”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Guo said: "Troops cannot be assembled; when assembled they cannot be made elite—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Troops won't assemble, and even if they do they won't be any good. What then?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“葵請視兩路之兵，別其精銳，君侯留三萬帳前，賊不敢動矣。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He said: "Kui asks to inspect the troops of both routes, sort out their elite, and if my lord keeps thirty thousand before the tent the bandits will not dare move."
translations.idiomatic: Kui replied: "Let me inspect the forces on both circuits and pick out the best. Keep thirty thousand at headquarters, and the rebels won't dare stir."

sentences.zh: 國曰：“不若集淮兵來閱，而君董之，既足示眾，亦可選銳。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Guo said: "Would it not be better to gather the Huai troops for review, with you supervising? That would both display strength to the masses and allow selection of the elite."
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Better to assemble the Huai troops for inspection under your direction. That would impress everyone and let us pick the best."

sentences.zh: 葵曰：“有 兵之郡，必當衝要，守將豈可空壁以從製使命耶？

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Kui said: "Every commandery with troops must guard a vital point—how can its defending general leave the walls empty to follow the pacification commissioner's order?
translations.idiomatic: Kui said: "Every garrisoned prefecture holds a critical post. How can its commander strip his walls bare to obey the pacification commissioner?

sentences.zh: 必將力爭於朝，分留自衛。

translations.literal: They are sure to struggle hard at court and keep part of their forces for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: They will fight it at court and hold troops back for their own defense.

sentences.zh: 一得朝命，必匿其強壯，遣老弱以備數。

translations.literal: Once they receive the court order, they are sure to hide their strong men and send the old and weak to make up the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court order comes, they will hide their best men and send the old and weak to fill the rolls.

sentences.zh: 本欲選銳，適得其鈍，本欲示眾，適示單弱， 徒啟戎心。”

translations.literal: Intending to select the elite, one gets only the dull; intending to display numbers, one displays weakness alone—this merely awakens the enemy's ambition.
translations.idiomatic: You mean to pick elites and will get dregs instead; you mean to show strength and will display weakness—nothing but an invitation to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 國不聽，卒敗。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Guo did not listen and was ultimately defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Guo would not listen and was defeated in the end.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，範知揚州，乞調葵以強勇、雄邊軍五千屯寶應備賊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing, Fan became prefect of Yangzhou and requested that Kui be transferred with five thousand troops of the Qiangyong and Xiongbian armies to garrison at Baoying against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoqing (1225) Fan became prefect of Yangzhou and asked that Kui be transferred with five thousand men from the Qiangyong and Xiongbian armies to hold Baoying against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 葵在廬州，數費私錢會諸將球射，與製置使曾式中不合，葵去之。

translations.literal: While Kui was at Luzhou he repeatedly spent his own money to gather the generals for ball games and archery; he did not get along with the pacification commissioner Zeng Shizhong, and Kui left the post.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou Kui often spent his own money entertaining the generals with ball games and archery. He fell out with pacification commissioner Zeng Shizhong and left the post.

sentences.zh: 言者以為擅，遂奉祠。

translations.literal: Memorialists deemed this overstepping authority, and he was given a sinecure temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called it overreach, and he was given a sinecure temple appointment.

sentences.zh: 三年，起為將作監丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled as assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 全造舟益急，葵復致書史彌遠曰：“李全既破鹽城，反稱陳知縣自棄城，蓋欲欺朝廷以款討罪之師，彼得一意修舟楫，造器械，窺伺城邑，或直浮海以搗腹心，此 其奸謀，明若觀火。

translations.literal: Quan built ships with increasing urgency; Kui again wrote to Shi Miyuan, saying: "Li Quan, having already taken Yancheng, now claims instead that Magistrate Chen abandoned the city of his own accord—clearly intending to deceive the court and stall the punitive army sent to punish his crime, so that he may devote himself wholly to building ships and making weapons, spying on cities, or even sailing straight across the sea to strike at the heartland. This treacherous design is as plain as watching fire.
translations.idiomatic: Quan redoubled his shipbuilding. Kui wrote again to Shi Miyuan: "Li Quan has taken Yancheng, yet claims Magistrate Chen abandoned it on his own— plainly to deceive the court and stall the punitive expedition while he builds ships, forges weapons, scouts our cities, or even sails straight across the sea to strike the heartland. His treachery is clear as daylight.

sentences.zh: 葵自聞鹽城失守，日夕延頸以俟製帥之設施，今乃聞遣王節入鹽城祈哀於逆。

translations.literal: Since Kui heard that Yancheng had fallen, day and night he stretched his neck awaiting measures from the pacification commander; now he hears instead that Wang Jie was sent into Yancheng to plead before the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Yancheng fell I have waited eagerly for action from the pacification commander. Now I hear Wang Jie was sent into Yancheng to plead with the rebel.

sentences.zh: 葵又聞遣二吏入山陽，請命於賊婦。

translations.literal: Kui also heard that two clerks were sent into Shanyang to request orders from the rebel's wife.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear two clerks were sent to Shanyang to take orders from the rebel's wife.

sentences.zh: 堂堂製閫，如此舉措，豈不墮 賊計，貽笑天下、貽笑外夷乎？

translations.literal: For so august a frontier command to take such measures—does this not fall into the bandits' scheme and bring ridicule upon the realm and upon foreign peoples?
translations.idiomatic: For a frontier command of such standing to act this way—does it not play into the rebels' hands and make us a laughingstock at home and abroad?

sentences.zh: 又聞張國明前此出山陽，已知賊將舉鹽城之兵，今若聽國明言，更從闊略，則自此人心解體，萬事渙散，社稷之憂有不可勝諱者。

translations.literal: It is also heard that Zhang Guoming, when he earlier left Shanyang, already knew the bandits would raise the Yancheng army; if his words are now followed and a broad indulgence is again adopted, from this point hearts will dissolve, all affairs scatter, and worries for the altars of state will be beyond concealment.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that when Zhang Guoming left Shanyang he already knew the rebels meant to march from Yancheng. If his counsel is followed and leniency prevails again, morale will collapse, order will unravel, and the danger to the realm will be beyond hiding.

sentences.zh: 葵 非欲張皇生事啟釁，李全決非忠臣，非孝子。

translations.literal: Kui does not wish to alarm and stir up trouble to provoke conflict; Li Quan is certainly no loyal minister and no filial son.
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean to alarm the court or manufacture a quarrel. Li Quan is no loyal subject and no filial son.

sentences.zh: 丞相苟聽葵之言，翻然改圖，發兵討叛，則豈獨可以強國勢安社稷，葵父子世受國恩，亦庶幾萬一之報。

translations.literal: If the chief councilor would heed Kui's words, suddenly change course, and dispatch troops to punish rebellion, then not only could national strength be fortified and the altars of state secured—Kui father and son, who for generations have received the state's grace, might also repay it in some small measure.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Excellency heeds me, changes course, and sends troops against the rebel, you will not only strengthen the realm and secure the altars of state—my father and I, who owe the dynasty a lifetime of favor, may at last repay it in some small way.

sentences.zh: 使丞相不聽葵 言，不發兵討賊，則豈特不可以強國勢安社稷，而葵亦不知死所，不復可報君相之恩矣。

translations.literal: If the chief councilor does not heed Kui's words and does not dispatch troops to punish the bandits, then not only can national strength not be fortified nor the altars secured—Kui also will not know where to die, and can no longer repay the grace of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Excellency refuses and sends no troops, you will not only fail to strengthen the realm—you will leave me with no place to die and no way left to repay the grace of throne and minister.

sentences.zh: 一安一危，一治一亂，係朝廷之討叛與不討爾。

translations.literal: One path leads to security, one to peril; one to order, one to chaos—it all depends on whether the court punishes rebellion or does not.
translations.idiomatic: Security or peril, order or chaos—all hinge on whether the court moves against the rebel.

sentences.zh: 淮東安則江南安，江南安則 社稷安，社稷安則丞相安，丞相安則凡為國之臣子、為丞相之門人弟子莫不安矣。”

translations.literal: If Huai East is secure then Jiangnan is secure; if Jiangnan is secure then the altars of state are secure; if the altars are secure then the chief councilor is secure; if the chief councilor is secure then every subject of the state and every disciple of the chief councilor's school is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Secure Huai East and Jiangnan is secure; secure Jiangnan and the realm is secure; secure the realm and Your Excellency is secure; secure Your Excellency and every subject and every man in your circle is secure.

sentences.zh: 又言於朝曰：“葵父子兄弟，世受國恩，每見外夷、盜賊侵侮國 家，未嚐不為忠憤所激。

translations.literal: He also addressed the court, saying: "Kui, father, sons, and brothers have for generations received the state's grace; whenever they see foreign peoples or bandits insult the state, they have never failed to be stirred by loyal indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized the court: "My father, brothers, and I have received the dynasty's favor for generations. Whenever barbarians or bandits insult the realm, loyal outrage has never failed to move us.

sentences.zh: 今大逆不道，邈視朝廷，負君相卵翼之恩，無如李全。

translations.literal: Now in great treason and impiety, treating the court with distant contempt and betraying the nurturing grace of lord and minister—none surpasses Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Today no one surpasses Li Quan in treason, in contempt for the court, or in betraying the sheltering grace of throne and minister.

sentences.zh: 前此畔逆未彰，猶可言也，今已破蕩城邑，略無忌憚，若朝廷更從隱忍，則將何以為 國？

translations.literal: Before this his rebellion was not yet manifest and one could still speak of restraint; now he has stormed and ravaged cities with scarcely any fear—if the court again follows forbearance, how can there still be a state?
translations.idiomatic: While his rebellion was still hidden, forbearance had some excuse. Now he has sacked cities without restraint. If the court indulges him further, what will remain of the state?

sentences.zh: 欲望特發剛斷，名其為賊，即日命將遣師，水陸並進，誅鋤此逆，以安社稷，以保生靈。

translations.literal: I desire that resolute judgment be specially issued, that he be named a bandit, and that on that very day generals be ordered and armies dispatched by land and water together to cut down and uproot this rebel, to secure the altars of state and protect the people.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the court to act with firm resolve: name him a rebel, dispatch generals and armies that very day by land and sea, destroy this traitor, secure the altars of state, and protect the people.

sentences.zh: 葵雖不才，願身許朝廷；

translations.literal: Though Kui lacks talent, he is willing to devote his person to the court;
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I offer my person to the court;

sentences.zh: 如或不然，乞將葵早賜處分，以安邊鄙，以便 國事。”

translations.literal: if otherwise, I beg that Kui be early granted disposition, to secure the frontier and facilitate state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I beg that I be dealt with at once, so the frontier may be settled and state business proceed.

sentences.zh: 彌遠猶未欲興討，參知政事鄭清之讚決之。

translations.literal: Miyuan still did not wish to launch a punitive campaign; Vice Grand Councilor Zheng Qingzhi approved and decided it.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan still hesitated to launch a campaign, but Vice Grand Councilor Zheng Qingzhi endorsed the decision.

sentences.zh: 乃加葵直寶章閣、淮東提點刑獄兼知滁州。

translations.literal: Kui was then promoted to direct attache of the Baozhang Pavilion, Huai East intendant of judicial inspection, and concurrent prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was then made direct attache of the Baozhang Pavilion, Huai East intendant of judicial inspection, and concurrent prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 範刻日約葵，葵帥雄勝、寧淮、武定、強勇步騎萬四 千，命王鑒、扈斌、胡顯等將之，以葵兼參議官。

translations.literal: Fan set a day and joined Kui; Kui commanded fourteen thousand infantry and cavalry of the Xiongsheng, Ninghuai, Wuding, and Qiangyong armies, appointing Wang Jian, Hu Bin, Hu Xian, and others to lead them, with Kui concurrently serving as planning officer.
translations.idiomatic: Fan fixed a date and joined Kui. Kui led fourteen thousand foot and horse from the Xiongsheng, Ninghuai, Wuding, and Qiangyong armies, with Wang Jian, Hu Bin, Hu Xian, and others as commanders and Kui as concurrent planning officer.

sentences.zh: 顯，穎之兄也，拳力絕人，方在襄陽，每出師必使顯及葵各領精銳分道赴戰，摧堅陷陣，聚散離合，前無勁敵，以 功至檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Xian was Ying's elder brother; his fist strength surpassed all men. When Fang was at Xiangyang, every time he marched out he had Xian and Kui each lead elite troops by separate routes into battle, breaking hard points and smashing formations, dispersing and gathering, parting and joining—before them no strong enemy stood; through merit he reached the rank of acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was Ying's elder brother, a man of superhuman strength. At Xiangyang Fang always sent Xian and Kui each with elite troops by separate routes—breaking lines, shattering formations, wheeling and regrouping with no worthy foe before them. For his service Xian rose to acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 已而，全攻揚州東門，葵親出搏戰。

translations.literal: Before long Quan attacked Yangzhou's east gate; Kui personally went out to grapple in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Quan attacked Yangzhou's east gate. Kui went out in person to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊將張友呼城門請葵出，及出，全在隔壕立馬相勞苦。

translations.literal: The bandit general Zhang You called at the gate asking Kui to come out; when he came out, Quan stood his horse across the moat and exchanged courteous words of concern.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Zhang You called at the gate for Kui. When Kui came out, Quan sat his horse across the moat and spoke to him with feigned cordiality.

sentences.zh: 左右欲射全，葵止之，問全來何為？

translations.literal: Those beside him wished to shoot Quan; Kui stopped them and asked what Quan had come for.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants wanted to shoot Quan, but Kui stopped them and asked why he had come.

sentences.zh: 全 曰：“朝廷動見猜疑，今復絕我糧餉，我非背叛，索錢糧耳。”

translations.literal: Quan said: "The court is always suspicious of me; now it has again cut off my provisions. I am not rebelling—I am only demanding money and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Quan said: "The court is always suspicious of me. Now you've cut off my supplies. I'm not rebelling—I only want money and grain."

sentences.zh: 葵曰：“朝廷資汝錢糧，寵汝官職，蓋不貲矣。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Kui said: "The court has supplied you with money and grain and favored you with office—surely the count is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said: "The court has lavished money, grain, and rank on you beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 待汝以忠臣孝子，而乃反戈攻陷城邑，朝廷安得不絕 汝錢糧。

translations.literal: It treated you as a loyal minister and filial son, yet you turned your weapons to attack and seize cities—how could the court not cut off your money and grain?
translations.idiomatic: It treated you as a loyal subject and filial son, yet you turned your blade and seized cities. How could the court keep feeding you?

sentences.zh: 汝雲非叛，欺人乎？

translations.literal: You say you are not rebelling—are you deceiving men?
translations.idiomatic: You say you're not rebelling—do you mean to fool men?

sentences.zh: 欺天乎？”

translations.literal: Deceiving Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Or Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 切責之言甚多，全無以對，彎弓抽矢向葵而去。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) His cutting rebukes were many; Quan had no reply, bent his bow, drew an arrow, and rode toward Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He heaped rebuke upon rebuke. Quan had no answer, strung his bow, nocked an arrow, and galloped at Kui.

sentences.zh: 於是數戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Thereafter in several battles all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: After that they won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 四年正月壬寅，遂殺全。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, day renyin, Quan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, on day renyin, Quan was killed.

sentences.zh: 事見《全傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the Quan biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Li Quan biography.

sentences.zh: 進葵福州觀察使、 左驍衛上將軍，葵辭不受。

translations.literal: Kui was promoted to observer of Fuzhou and senior general of the Left Xiaowei Guard; Kui declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was promoted to observer of Fuzhou and senior general of the Left Xiaowei Guard, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 八月，召封樞密院稟議，受寶章閣待制、樞密副都承旨，依舊職仍落起復，尋進兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was summoned to seal and report at the Bureau of Military Affairs, received appointment as Baozhang Pavilion academician-in-waiting and deputy chief receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retained his former posts while shedding the mourning recall status, and soon was advanced to vice-minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was summoned to the Bureau of Military Affairs, accepted appointment as Baozhang Pavilion academician-in-waiting and deputy chief receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs, kept his former posts while shedding mourning recall status, and was soon promoted to vice-minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，詔授淮東製置使兼知揚州，入對，帝曰：“卿父子兄弟，宣力甚多，卿在行陣又能率先士卒，捐身報國，此尤儒臣之所難，朕甚嘉之。”

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year an edict appointed him commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission and concurrent prefect of Yangzhou. Entering audience, the Emperor said: "Your father, sons, and brothers have rendered much service; you in the battle line can also lead the soldiers first and give your body to repay the state—this is especially hard for scholar-officials; I greatly commend it."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he was appointed commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission and concurrent prefect of Yangzhou. At audience the Emperor said: "Your father, brothers, and you have served the realm well. In battle you lead from the front and risk your life for the state—rare even among scholar-officials. I commend you highly."

sentences.zh: 葵頓首謝曰：“臣不佞，忠孝之義，嚐奉教於君子，世受國恩，當捐軀以報陛下。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Kui bowed his head in thanks and said: "Your subject lacks talent; the principles of loyalty and filial piety I have received instruction in from gentlemen; having for generations received the state's grace, I ought to give my body to repay Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed and replied: "I am unworthy. Gentlemen have taught me loyalty and filial piety. My family has received the dynasty's favor for generations. I should give my life to repay Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，朝議收復三京，葵上疏請出戰，乃授權兵部尚書、京河製置使，知應天府、南京留守兼淮東製置使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping the court debated recovering the Three Capitals; Kui submitted a memorial requesting to go out to battle, and was appointed acting minister of War, commissioner of the Jing-He Pacification Commission, prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, Nanjing regent, and concurrent commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping (1234) the court debated retaking the Three Capitals. Kui memorialized asking to take the field and was appointed acting minister of War, commissioner of the Jing-He Pacification Commission, prefect of Yingtian, Nanjing regent, and concurrent Huai East pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時盛暑行師，汴堤破決，水潦泛溢，糧運不繼，所 復州郡，皆空城，無兵食可因。

translations.literal: At that time they marched in the height of summer; the Bian embankment burst, floodwaters spread everywhere, grain transport could not keep up, and every prefecture and commandery recovered was an empty city with no troops or provisions to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: They marched in the height of summer. The Bian dike broke, floods spread, supplies failed, and every city they retook was empty—no troops, no grain to sustain them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北兵南下，渡河，發水閘，兵多溺死，遂潰而歸。

translations.literal: Before long northern troops came south, crossed the river, opened the sluice gates, and many soldiers drowned; they then broke and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long northern troops came south, crossed the river, and opened the sluice gates. Many men drowned, the army broke, and they retreated.

sentences.zh: 範上表劾葵，詔與全子才各降一秩，授兵部侍郎、淮東製置使，移司泗州。

translations.literal: Fan submitted a memorial impeaching Kui; an edict demoted him and Quan Zicai each one rank, appointed him vice-minister of War and commissioner of the Huai East Pacification Commission, and moved his headquarters to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan impeached Kui. An edict demoted him and Quan Zicai each one rank, reappointed him vice-minister of War and Huai East pacification commissioner, and moved his headquarters to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，以寶章閣學士知揚州，依舊制置使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi he was made Baozhang Pavilion academician and prefect of Yangzhou, retaining his pacification commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaxi (1237) he became Baozhang Pavilion academician and prefect of Yangzhou, keeping his pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 二年，以應援安豐捷，奏拜刑部尚書，進端明殿學士，特予執政恩例，復兼本路屯田使。

translations.literal: In the second year, for the victory in relieving Anfeng, he was memorialized for appointment as minister of Justice, advanced to academician of the Duanming Hall, specially granted the favor normally given to chief councilors, and again made concurrent intendant of agriculture for the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, for the victory at Anfeng, he was promoted to minister of Justice and academician of the Duanming Hall, granted chief-councilor privileges, and again made concurrent intendant of agriculture for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 葵前後留揚八年，墾田治兵，邊備益飭。

translations.literal: Kui altogether remained at Yangzhou eight years, opening fields and drilling troops; frontier defenses grew ever more orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Kui spent eight years at Yangzhou in all, opening land and drilling troops until frontier defenses were thoroughly restored.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，進大學士、知潭州、湖南安撫使，改福州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he was advanced to grand academician, prefect of Tanzhou, and pacification commissioner of Hunan, then transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunyou (1242) he was made grand academician, prefect of Tanzhou, and Hunan pacification commissioner, then transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，葬其母，乞追服終製，不允。

translations.literal: In the third year he buried his mother and begged to resume mourning and complete the full term; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he buried his mother and asked to resume full mourning; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 葵上疏曰：“移忠為孝，臣子之通誼；

translations.literal: Kui submitted a memorial, saying: "Shifting loyalty to serve as filial piety is the common principle of subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Kui memorialized: "To shift loyalty into filial duty is the common obligation of a subject;

sentences.zh: 教孝求忠，君父之至仁。

translations.literal: teaching filial piety to seek loyalty is the utmost benevolence of lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: to teach filial piety in order to win loyalty is the deepest kindness of ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 忠孝一原，並行不悖。

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety spring from one root and proceed together without conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety share one root and need not conflict.

sentences.zh: 故曰忠臣以事其君，孝子以事其親，其 本一也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that the loyal minister serves his lord and the filial son serves his parent—their root is one.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, the loyal minister serves his ruler and the filial son serves his parent—the root is the same.

sentences.zh: 臣不佞，戒謹持循，惟恐先墜。

translations.literal: Your subject lacks talent; he guards himself with caution and holds to propriety, fearing only to fall short first.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy. I have tried to live carefully, fearing only to fall short.

sentences.zh: 往歲叨當事任，服在戎行，偕同氣以率先，冒萬死而不顧，捐軀戡難，效命守封，是以孝事君之充也。

translations.literal: In past years I presumptuously held office, served in the army, joined my brothers in leading the way, braved ten thousand deaths without regard, gave my body to quell hardship, and devoted my life to guarding the frontier—this was the fulfillment of serving the lord through filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In past years I held office and served in the field, marching with my brothers at the fore, risking death without hesitation, giving my body to quell disaster and my life to guard the frontier—that was filial service to the throne in full.

sentences.zh: 陛下昭示顯揚，優崇 寵數，使為人子者感恩，為人親者知勸矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty displayed and exalted this, bestowing generous favor and rank, so that those who are sons feel gratitude and those who are parents know encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has honored this openly with generous favor, so that sons feel gratitude and parents take heart.

sentences.zh: 臣昨於草土，被命起家，勉從權製，先國家之急而後親喪也。

translations.literal: Your subject, lately in the grass and dust of mourning, received orders to leave home and take office, striving to follow the provisional rule, putting the state's urgency first and parental bereavement after.
translations.idiomatic: When I was still in mourning dust I was ordered back to office. I accepted the exceptional rule and put the state's urgency before my grief.

sentences.zh: 今釋位去官，已追服居廬，乞從彝製。”

translations.literal: Now having relinquished rank and left office, I have resumed mourning and dwell in the mourning hut; I beg to follow the standard rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have left office, resumed mourning, and dwell in the mourning hut. I beg to follow the proper rites."

sentences.zh: 又不許。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Again this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Again the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 再上疏 曰：“臣昔者奉詔討逆，適丁家難，閔然哀疚之中，命以驅馳之事，移孝為忠，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject formerly received orders to punish rebellion just as a family calamity struck; amid grieving sorrow he was charged with urgent service on the road—shifting filial piety to loyalty, he did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "When I was ordered to punish rebellion, a family calamity struck. In grief I was sent on urgent service—shifting filial duty into loyal service, I did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 是臣嚐先國家之急，而效臣子之義矣。

translations.literal: Thus your subject has already put the state's urgency first and fulfilled a subject's duty.
translations.idiomatic: I have already put the state first and done a subject's duty.

sentences.zh: 親恩未報，浸逾一紀，食稻衣錦， 俯仰增愧。

translations.literal: Parental grace remains unrequited; more than a full cycle has passed while eating rice and wearing brocade—in every glance shame increases.
translations.idiomatic: My parents' grace remains unrepaid. More than twelve years have passed while I eat fine rice and wear brocade—every moment fills me with shame.

sentences.zh: 且臣業已追衰麻之製，伸苫塊之哀，負土成墳，倚廬待盡，喪事有進而無退，固不應數月而除也。”

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has already resumed the hemp garments of mourning, expressed grief upon the mourning mat, carried earth to complete the tomb, and leans upon the hut awaiting the end—mourning rites advance and do not retreat; they surely should not be ended after only a few months.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have resumed hemp mourning, grieved upon the mourning mat, carried earth to raise the tomb, and dwell in the hut awaiting death's end. Mourning moves forward and never back—it cannot rightly end after only a few months."

sentences.zh: 乃命提舉洞霄宮，不拜。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He was then ordered to serve as intendant of the Dongxiao Palace; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed intendant of the Dongxiao Palace but declined.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，授 同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he was appointed vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunyou (1244) he was appointed vice-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：“今天下之事，其大者有幾？

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated: "Of affairs under Heaven today, how many are there of the greatest importance?
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Of all affairs under Heaven today, how many are truly great?

sentences.zh: 天下之才，其可用者有幾？

translations.literal: Of talents under Heaven, how many are there that can be used?
translations.idiomatic: Of all talent under Heaven, how much is truly usable?

sentences.zh: 吾從其大者而講明之，疏其可用者而任使之。

translations.literal: Let us take the greatest and clarify them; sort out those who can be used and appoint and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Let us clarify the greatest matters and appoint the usable men.

sentences.zh: 有勇略者治兵，有心計者治財，寬厚者 任牧養，剛正者持風憲。

translations.literal: Let those with courage and strategy administer troops; those with resourceful plans administer finances; the generous and broad-minded be charged with nurturing the people; the upright and firm hold the censorial law.
translations.idiomatic: Men of courage and strategy should command armies; men of shrewd planning should manage finances; the generous should govern and nurture the people; the upright should uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 為官擇人，不為人而擇官。

translations.literal: Choose men for office, do not choose offices for men.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men to fit the office, not offices to fit the men.

sentences.zh: 用之既當，任之既久，然後可以責其成效。”

translations.literal: Once they are employed fittingly and entrusted for long enough, only then can one demand results from them.
translations.idiomatic: Only when men are rightly appointed and kept in post long enough can their performance be judged."

sentences.zh: 又乞“亟與宰臣講求規畫，凡有關於宗社安危治亂之大計者條具以 聞，審其所先後緩急以圖籌策，則治功可成，外患不足畏”。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He also begged, "Urgently consult with the chief ministers to plan and scheme; for every great policy bearing on the altars of state, security and peril, order and disorder, set them forth item by item for report; consider what comes first and last, urgent and delayed, in order to devise strategy—then governing achievement can be completed and external threat need not be feared."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the court to "consult urgently with the chief ministers on overall planning—list every major policy affecting the dynasty's survival, weigh priorities and urgency in forming strategy, and governing success will follow while external threats need not be feared."

sentences.zh: 又乞“創遊擊軍三萬人以防江”。

translations.literal: He also begged to "raise a mobile army of thirty thousand to guard the river."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to raise a mobile force of thirty thousand to defend the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his requests.

sentences.zh: 十二月，拜知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrent vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was made director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 又特授樞密使兼參知政 事、督視江、淮、京西、湖北軍馬，封長沙郡公。

translations.literal: He was also specially appointed commissioner of military affairs and concurrent vice grand councilor, with oversight of armies and horses in Jiang, Huai, Jingxi, and Hubei, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was also specially made commissioner of military affairs and vice grand councilor, with oversight of forces in the Jiang, Huai, Jingxi, and Hubei regions, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 尋知建康府、行宮留守、江東安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Jiankang Prefecture, regent of the traveling palace, and pacification commissioner of Jiang East.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became prefect of Jiankang, regent of the traveling palace, and Jiang East pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，特授光祿大夫、右丞相兼樞密使，封信國公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was specially appointed Grandee of Splendid Happiness, right chief councilor and concurrent commissioner of military affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was specially made Grandee of Splendid Happiness, right chief councilor and commissioner of military affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xinguo.

sentences.zh: 四上表力 辭，言者以宰相須用讀書人，罷為觀文殿學士，充醴泉觀使兼侍讀，仍奉朝請。

translations.literal: Four times he submitted memorials forcefully declining; critics held that a chief councilor must be a man of letters; he was dismissed to academician of the Guanwen Hall, made intendant of the Liquan Abbey and concurrent reader-in-attendance, and still attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four memorials forcefully declining. Critics argued that a chief councilor must be a scholar-official, so he was removed to academician of the Guanwen Hall, made intendant of the Liquan Abbey and reader-in-attendance, and retained court audience privileges.

sentences.zh: 尋判潭州、湖南安撫使，加特進。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned as prefect of Tanzhou and pacification commissioner of Hunan, and granted special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to Tanzhou as Hunan pacification commissioner and granted special advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 寶祐二年，宜撫廣西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyou he was appointed pacification commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoyou (1254) he was made pacification commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，改鎮荊湖，城荊門及 郢州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to command Jinghu, and fortified Jingmen and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to command the Jinghu region and fortified Jingmen and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 改授湖南路安撫使、判潭州，再辭，依舊職醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as pacification commissioner of Hunan Circuit and prefect of Tanzhou; he declined again and retained his former post as intendant of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Hunan pacification commissioner and prefect of Tanzhou, declined again, and kept his post as intendant of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 五年，進少保、寧遠軍節度使，進封魏國公、醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to Junior Guardian and military governor of the Ningyuan Army, further enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, and made intendant of the Liquan Abbey and concurrent reader-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Junior Guardian and military governor of the Ningyuan Army, further enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, and made intendant of the Liquan Abbey and reader-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 四辭，免。

translations.literal: Four times he declined; the appointments were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He declined four times and the appointments were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，判慶元府、沿海 製置使，尋授沿江、江東宣撫使，置司建康府，任責隆興府、饒州江州徽州兩界防拓調遣，時暫兼判建康府、行宮留守，尋授江東西宣撫使，節製調遣饒、信、袁、 臨江、撫、吉、隆興官軍民兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing he was assigned as prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture and coastal pacification commissioner; soon he was appointed riverine and Jiang East pacification commissioner, with headquarters at Jiankang Prefecture, charged with defense and deployment across the boundary of Longxing Prefecture, Raozhou, Jiangzhou, and Huizhou; for a time he concurrently served as prefect of Jiankang and regent of the traveling palace; soon he was appointed pacification commissioner of Jiang East and West, with authority to command regular and militia forces of Rao, Xin, Yuan, Linjiang, Fu, Ji, and Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiqing (1259) he was assigned to Qingyuan and made coastal pacification commissioner. Soon he became riverine and Jiang East pacification commissioner with headquarters at Jiankang, charged with frontier defense and deployment between Longxing, Raozhou, Jiangzhou, and Huizhou. For a time he also served as prefect of Jiankang and regent of the traveling palace. He was then made pacification commissioner of Jiang East and West, with authority over regular and militia forces in Rao, Xin, Yuan, Linjiang, Fu, Ji, and Longxing.

sentences.zh: 訪問百姓疾苦，罷行黜陟，並許便宜從事。

translations.literal: He was to inquire into the people's hardships, suspend promotions and demotions, and was permitted to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was to inquire into the people's hardships, suspend routine promotions and demotions, and act at his discretion as needed.

sentences.zh: 範字武仲，少從父軍中。

translations.literal: Fan, courtesy name Wuzhong, in youth followed his father in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, courtesy name Wuzhong, followed his father into the army from youth.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年，嚐與弟葵殲金人於高頭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading he once joined his younger brother Kui in annihilating Jin troops at Gaotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiading (1220) he and his younger brother Kui annihilated Jin forces at Gaotou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出師唐、鄧，範與葵監軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the army marched out to Tang and Deng; Fan and Kui supervised the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the army marched on Tang and Deng; Fan and Kui served as army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 孟宗政時知棗陽，憚於供億，使人問曰：“金人在蘄、黃，而 君攻唐、鄧，何也？”

translations.literal: Meng Zongzheng was then prefect of Zaoyang and feared the burden of supply; he sent someone to ask, saying: "The Jin are at Qi and Huang—why do you attack Tang and Deng?"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zongzheng, then prefect of Zaoyang, feared the supply burden and sent someone to ask: "The Jin are at Qi and Huang—why are you attacking Tang and Deng?"

sentences.zh: 範曰：“不然，徹襄陽之備以救蘄、黃，則唐、鄧必將躡吾後。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Fan said: "Not so. If we withdraw Xiangyang's defenses to relieve Qi and Huang, then Tang and Deng will surely tread on our rear.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "Not so. If we strip Xiangyang's defenses to save Qi and Huang, Tang and Deng will strike at our rear.

sentences.zh: 且蘄、黃之寇正銳，曷若先搗唐、鄧以示有餘，唐、鄧應我之不暇，則吾圉不 守而自固，寇在蘄、黃師日以老，然後回師蹙之，可勝敵而無後患。”

translations.literal: Moreover the enemy at Qi and Huang is at its sharpest—how much better to strike Tang and Deng first to show we have strength to spare; when Tang and Deng must answer us and have no leisure, then our defenses need not be held and will secure themselves; the enemy at Qi and Huang will day by day grow weary, and then we can wheel our army to press them— we can defeat the enemy without later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the enemy at Qi and Huang is at peak strength. Better to hit Tang and Deng first to show we still have reserves. When Tang and Deng must respond and cannot spare forces, our defenses will hold themselves. The Qi-Huang enemy will wear down day by day, and then we can turn and crush them—victory without lingering danger."

sentences.zh: 又敗金人於久長，與弟葵俱授製置安撫司內機，事具《葵傳》。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He again defeated Jin troops at Jiuchang; he and his younger brother Kui were both appointed internal planners of the Pacification Commission; the affair is fully recorded in the Kui biography.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Jin forces at Jiuchang. He and his brother Kui were both made internal planners of the pacification commission. The full account appears in the Kui biography.

sentences.zh: 十五年，丁父 憂，起復直秘閣、通判揚州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he mourned his father's death, was recalled from mourning as direct attache of the Secretariat Pavilion, and made vice-prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, after his father's death, he was recalled from mourning as direct attache of the Secretariat Pavilion and vice-prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，為軍器監丞，以直秘閣知光州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments and, as direct attache of the Secretariat Pavilion, was made prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments and, as direct attache of the Secretariat Pavilion, prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入為知大宗正丞、刑部侍郎、試將作監兼權知鎮江府。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, vice-minister of Justice, acting director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and concurrent acting prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, vice-minister of Justice, acting director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and acting prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 進直徽猷閣、知揚州、淮東安 撫副使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to direct attache of the Huiyou Pavilion, prefect of Yangzhou, and deputy pacification commissioner of Huai East.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct attache of the Huiyou Pavilion, prefect of Yangzhou, and deputy Huai East pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 劉全、王文信二軍老幼留揚州，範欲修軍政，懼其徒漏泄兵機，乃時饋勞。

translations.literal: The armies of Liu Quan and Wang Wenxin, old and young, remained at Yangzhou; Fan wished to reform military administration but feared their followers would leak military secrets, so he periodically sent gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Liu Quan and Wang Wenxin, with their families, remained at Yangzhou. Fan wanted to reform military administration but feared their men would leak military secrets, so he sent periodic gifts and rewards.

sentences.zh: 二家既大喜，範即遺徐晞稷書，令教二人挈家歸楚，二人從之，範厚賚以遣。

translations.literal: Once both families were greatly pleased, Fan sent a letter to Xu Xiji ordering him to instruct the two men to take their families back to Chu; the two complied, and Fan generously rewarded them and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: When both families were well pleased, Fan wrote to Xu Xiji instructing the two commanders to move their families back to Chu. They complied, and Fan rewarded them generously and sent them off.

sentences.zh: 有 孫海者，其眾亦八百。

translations.literal: There was one Sun Hai, whose followers also numbered eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: One Sun Hai also had eight hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 範並請抽還楚州，又請創馬軍三千，招遊手之強壯者及籍牢城重役人充之。

translations.literal: Fan also requested that he be withdrawn to Chuzhou, and further requested the creation of three thousand cavalry, recruiting strong idlers and registering men on heavy corvée for fortress duty to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Fan also asked to withdraw Sun Hai to Chuzhou and requested three thousand new cavalry, recruiting strong idlers and men on heavy fortress corvée to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 別籍民為半年兵，春夏在田，秋冬教閱。

translations.literal: He separately registered the people as half-year soldiers—working fields in spring and summer, drilling in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: He registered civilians as half-year soldiers who farmed in spring and summer and drilled in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 官免建砦而私不廢農。

translations.literal: The state was spared building camps while private households did not abandon farming.
translations.idiomatic: The state need not build camps, and farming was not disrupted.

sentences.zh: 彭義斌使統領張士顯見範，請合謀討李全。

translations.literal: Peng Yibin sent his commander Zhang Shixian to see Fan and request a joint plan to attack Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yibin sent his commander Zhang Shixian to Fan to propose a joint campaign against Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 範告於製置使趙善湘曰：“以義斌蹙全，如山壓卵；

translations.literal: Fan reported to Pacification Commissioner Zhao Shanxiang, saying: "For Yibin to press Quan would be like a mountain crushing an egg;
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Pacification Commissioner Zhao Shanxiang: "Yibin pressing Quan would be like a mountain crushing an egg;

sentences.zh: 然必請而後討者，知有朝廷也。

translations.literal: yet he must request permission before attacking—this shows he knows there is a court.
translations.idiomatic: yet he asks permission before attacking—he knows there is a court above him.

sentences.zh: 失此不右，而右凶徒，則權綱解紐 矣。

translations.literal: If we fail to support this and instead support the vicious bandit, then the bonds of authority will come undone.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to support this and instead back the villain, the bonds of authority will unravel.

sentences.zh: 萬一義斌無朝命而成大勳，是又唐藩鎮之事，非計之得也。

translations.literal: If by chance Yibin wins a great merit without a court order, that would again be a Tang frontier garrison affair—not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: If Yibin wins a great victory without court orders, we will have another Tang-style warlord on our hands—not a sound plan.

sentences.zh: 莫若移揚州增戍之兵往盱眙，而四總管兵各留半以備金人，餘皆起發，擇一能將統之，命葵摘淮西精 銳萬人與會於楚州，出許浦海道，五十艘入淮，以斷賊歸路，密約義斌自北攻之，事無不濟。

translations.literal: Better to shift Yangzhou's reinforced garrison to Xuyi, while each of the four commanders-in-chief keeps half his troops to guard against the Jin and sends the rest forth, choose one capable general to command them, order Kui to detach ten thousand elite troops from Huai West to rendezvous at Chuzhou, send fifty ships from the Xupu sea route into the Huai to cut the bandits' line of retreat, and secretly arrange for Yibin to attack from the north—then nothing would fail.
translations.idiomatic: Better to shift Yangzhou's reinforcements to Xuyi, have each of the four commanders-in-chief keep half his force against the Jin and send the rest, choose one capable general to lead them, order Kui to bring ten thousand Huai West elites to Chuzhou, send fifty ships from Xupu into the Huai to cut the rebels' retreat, and secretly have Yibin attack from the north—nothing would fail.

sentences.zh: 四總管權位相侔，劉卓雖能得其歡心，而不能製其死命。

translations.literal: The four commanders-in-chief are equal in rank and power; although Liu Zhuo can win their goodwill, he cannot control their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The four commanders are equals in rank. Liu Zhuo may win their goodwill but cannot command their absolute obedience.

sentences.zh: 如用卓，須令 親履行陣，指蹤四人，不可止坐籌帷幄也。”

translations.literal: If Zhuo is used, he must personally walk the battle lines and direct the four men—he cannot merely sit planning within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhuo is chosen, he must lead in person on the field and direct all four commanders—not merely sit planning in the tent."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 範又曰：“國家討賊則自此中興，否則自此不振。

translations.literal: Fan also said: "If the state punishes the bandits, from this it will revive; if not, from this it will never recover.
translations.idiomatic: Fan added: "If the state punishes these rebels, the dynasty revives from this moment; if not, it never recovers.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷不欲張皇，則範乃提刑，職在捕盜，但令 範以本路兵措置楚州鹽賊，範當調時青、張惠兩軍之半，及其船數百，徑薄楚城，以遏賊路，調夏全、範成進之半，據漣、海而守之，又移揚州之戍以戍盱眙。

translations.literal: If the court does not wish to make a show of force, then Fan is merely judicial intendant—his duty is to capture bandits. Simply order Fan to deploy this circuit's troops against the salt bandits of Chuzhou; Fan should mobilize half the armies of Shi Qing and Zhang Hui, with their several hundred ships, to press directly on Chu city and block the bandits' route; mobilize half the forces of Xia Quan and Fan Chengjin to hold Lian and Hai; and shift Yangzhou's garrison to guard Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not want a large show of force, Fan is only a judicial intendant whose duty is to capture bandits. Order Fan to deploy this circuit's troops against the Chuzhou salt rebels. Fan would mobilize half the forces of Shi Qing and Zhang Hui with their several hundred ships to press Chu city and block the rebels' route, half the forces of Xia Quan and Fan Chengjin to hold Lian and Hai, and shift Yangzhou's garrison to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 然得 親提精銳雄勝、強勇等就時青於城外，示賊以形勢，諭賊以禍福，賊必自降。

translations.literal: Then, personally leading elite troops of Xiongsheng, Qiangyong, and the like to join Shi Qing outside the walls, show the bandits the situation and instruct them in fortune and disaster—the bandits will surely surrender of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then Fan would personally lead elite Xiongsheng and Qiangyong troops to join Shi Qing outside the walls, show the rebels the situation, and warn them of the consequences—they would surely surrender.

sentences.zh: 若猶拒守，則南北軍民雜處，必有內應者矣。

translations.literal: If they still resist and hold out, then with northern and southern troops and civilians mixed together, there will surely be those who respond from within.
translations.idiomatic: If they still resist, with northern and southern troops and civilians mixed together, there will surely be collaborators within.

sentences.zh: 別約義斌攻之於北，山陽下則進駐漣、海 以應之，撫歸附家屬以離其黨，不出半月，此賊必亡。

translations.literal: Separately arrange for Yibin to attack from the north; below Shanyang advance and encamp at Lian and Hai to respond; soothe the families of those who submit to split their faction—within half a month these bandits will surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: Arrange for Yibin to attack from the north; advance below Shanyang to Lian and Hai in support; win over the families of defectors to split their faction—and within half a month the rebels will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 若是，則不調許浦水軍，但得趙葵三千人亦足矣。

translations.literal: If so, then there is no need to mobilize the Xupu naval force—even three thousand men under Zhao Kui would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: In that case there is no need for the Xupu navy—even three thousand men under Zhao Kui would suffice.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷憚費，則全有預買軍需錢二十萬在真州，且漣、楚積 聚，多自足用。”

translations.literal: If the court fears expense, Quan has two hundred thousand in advance-purchase military funds at Zhenzhou, and moreover Lian and Chu have stores—much is self-sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: If the court fears expense, Quan has two hundred thousand in advance military funds at Zhenzhou, and Lian and Chu have ample stores on hand.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠報範書，令諭四總管各享安靖之福。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan replied to Fan in a letter, ordering him to instruct the four commanders-in-chief each to enjoy the blessings of peace and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan wrote back to Fan instructing him to tell the four commanders-in-chief to enjoy their peace and quiet.

sentences.zh: 範所遣計議官聞之，曰：“但恐禍根轉深，不得安靖爾。”

translations.literal: The planning officer Fan had sent, hearing this, said: "I fear only that the root of disaster will grow deeper and peace and quiet will not be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: The planning officer Fan had sent, hearing this, said: "I fear the root of disaster will only grow deeper, and there will be no peace."

sentences.zh: 各揮涕而歸。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Each wiped away tears and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Each wiped away tears and returned.

sentences.zh: 會全且至， 範又獻計曰：“撫機不發，事已無及。

translations.literal: When Quan was about to arrive, Fan again offered a plan, saying: "The moment for conciliation was not seized—already it is too late.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan was about to arrive, Fan offered another plan: "The moment for conciliation was missed—it is already too late.

sentences.zh: 侯景困喪河南，致毒蕭氏；

translations.literal: Hou Jing, defeated and bereft in Henan, brought poison upon the Xiao clan;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, defeated in Henan, brought ruin upon the Liang;

sentences.zh: 今逆全不得誌於義斌，而復慮四總管應之，歸據舊巢，其謀必急。

translations.literal: now the rebel Quan, unable to achieve his aim against Yibin and again fearing the four commanders-in-chief will respond, will return and hold his old nest—his plotting will surely be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: now the rebel Quan, thwarted by Yibin and fearing the four commanders will respond, will return to his old base—his scheming will be desperate.

sentences.zh: 然蹙之於喪敗之餘者易，圖之於 休息之後者難；

translations.literal: Yet to press him while he is still in defeat and loss is easy; to plot against him after he has rested is hard;
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is easy to crush him while he is still reeling from defeat, and hard to strike after he has recovered;

sentences.zh: 矧四總管合謀章露，必難遂已。

translations.literal: moreover the four commanders-in-chief's joint plot has been exposed in writing—it surely cannot easily be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the four commanders' joint plot is now exposed in writing—it cannot easily be undone.

sentences.zh: 但事機既變，局麵不同。

translations.literal: But the opportunity has already changed and the situation is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: But circumstances have changed and the situation is different.

sentences.zh: 若廟算果定，不欲出教令，但得密賜指授，範一切伏藏不動，隻約義斌，使自彼攻其所必 救，則機會在我，而前日之策可用矣。”

translations.literal: If the court's calculation is truly settled and you do not wish to issue an edict, but will secretly grant instructions, Fan will keep everything hidden and unmoving and only arrange with Yibin to have him attack from there what Quan must surely rescue—then the opportunity will be in our hands and yesterday's plan can be used.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's plan is settled and you do not wish to issue a public order, but will secretly instruct me, Fan will keep everything concealed and only coordinate with Yibin to attack what Quan must rescue—then the initiative will be ours and yesterday's plan can still work."

sentences.zh: 還報，戒範無出位專兵。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The reply came back warning Fan not to overstep his position and command troops on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The reply came back warning Fan not to overstep his authority and take independent command of troops.

sentences.zh: 範乃為書謝廟堂，且決之曰：“今上自一人，下至公卿百執事，又下至士民軍吏，無 不知禍賊之必反。

translations.literal: Fan then wrote a letter thanking the court and declaring decisively: "From the ruler above down to the hundred officials and functionaries, and further down to gentry, commoners, and military officers—none do not know that the disaster-bringing bandit will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Fan then wrote to thank the court and declared: "From the Emperor down through every official and clerk, and on to gentry, commoners, and military officers—everyone knows this villain will rebel.

sentences.zh: 雖先生之心，亦自知其必反也。

translations.literal: Even in Your Excellency's heart, you too know he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Even Your Excellency knows in your heart that he will rebel.

sentences.zh: 眾人知之則言之，先生知而獨不言，不言誠是也。

translations.literal: When the multitude knows, they speak; Your Excellency knows yet alone does not speak—not speaking is indeed right.
translations.idiomatic: When others know, they speak out. Your Excellency knows yet alone stays silent—and silence is indeed the wiser course.

sentences.zh: 內無臥薪嚐膽之誌，外無戰勝攻取之備，先生隱忍不言而徐思所 以製之，此廟謨所以為高也。

translations.literal: Within there is no resolve to sleep on brushwood and taste gall; without there are no preparations for victory in battle and storming cities—Your Excellency bears it in silence and slowly considers how to control him; this is why the court's strategy is so lofty.
translations.idiomatic: There is no resolve within to endure hardship for revenge, nor preparation without for victory in battle. Your Excellency bears it in silence and slowly considers how to control him—this is why the court's strategy is so lofty.

sentences.zh: 然以撫定責之晞稷，而以鎮守責之範。

translations.literal: Yet the duty of pacification and settlement is charged to Xiji, while the duty of garrison defense is charged to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pacification is Xiji's responsibility, while defense is Fan's.

sentences.zh: 責晞稷者函人之事也，責範者矢人之事也。

translations.literal: Charging Xiji is the coffin-maker's affair; charging Fan is the arrow-maker's affair.
translations.idiomatic: Charging Xiji is the coffin-maker's task; charging Fan is the arrow-maker's task.

sentences.zh: 既責範以惟恐不傷人之事，又禁其為傷人之痛，惡其 為傷人之言，何哉？

translations.literal: Having charged Fan with the task of fearing only that men are not wounded, yet forbidding him the pain of wounding men and hating his words about wounding men—why?
translations.idiomatic: You charge Fan with ensuring no one is hurt, yet forbid him to inflict pain, and hate his words about hurting anyone—why?

sentences.zh: 其禍賊見範為備，則必忌而不得以肆其奸，他日必將指範為首禍激變之人，劫朝廷以去範。

translations.literal: When the disaster-bringing bandit sees Fan making preparations, he will surely resent it and be unable to unleash his treachery; another day he will surely point to Fan as the man who first brought disaster and incited rebellion, and coerce the court to remove Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When the villain sees Fan preparing against him, he will resent it and be unable to act freely. One day he will denounce Fan as the man who first stirred trouble and incited rebellion, and coerce the court into removing Fan.

sentences.zh: 先生始未之信也，左右曰可，卿大夫曰可，先生必將 曰：‘是何惜一趙範而不以紓禍哉？

translations.literal: Your Excellency at first will not believe it; those at your side will say it is acceptable, the ministers will say it is acceptable, and Your Excellency will surely say: 'Why begrudge one Zhao Fan and not use him to relieve disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency will not believe it at first. Your attendants will say yes, the ministers will say yes, and Your Excellency will surely say: 'Why spare one Zhao Fan when surrendering him would avert disaster?

sentences.zh: ’必將縛範以授賊，而範遂為宋晁錯。

translations.literal: 'You will surely bind Fan and hand him to the bandits, and Fan will become the Song dynasty's Chao Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: 'You will bind Fan and hand him to the rebels, and Fan will become the Song dynasty's Chao Cuo.

sentences.zh: 雖然，使以範授賊而果足以紓國禍，範死何害哉？

translations.literal: Even so, if handing Fan to the bandits would truly suffice to relieve the state's disaster, what harm would Fan's death be?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, if surrendering Fan would truly avert national disaster, what harm in Fan's death?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：‘護家之狗，盜賊所惡。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'The dog that guards the house is what thieves hate.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: 'The dog that guards the house is what thieves hate.

sentences.zh: ’故盜 賊見有護家之狗，必將指斥於主人，使先去之，然後肆穿窬之奸而無所忌。

translations.literal: 'Therefore when thieves see a dog that guards the house, they will surely denounce it to the master and make him remove it first—then they can freely commit burglary without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: 'When thieves see a guard dog, they denounce it to the master and make him remove it first—then they can break in without fear.

sentences.zh: 然則殺犬固無益於弭盜也。

translations.literal: Then killing the dog is of no use in stopping theft.
translations.idiomatic: Killing the dog does nothing to stop the theft.

sentences.zh: 欲望矜憐，別與閑慢差遣。”

translations.literal: I beg for compassion and a separate, leisurely appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg for your compassion and a separate, less demanding appointment."

sentences.zh: 彌遠得書，為之動心。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Miyuan received the letter and was moved by it.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan received the letter and was moved.

sentences.zh: 二年春，奉祠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he received a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he received a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 三年，知安慶府，未行，改知池州，繼兼江東提舉常平。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made prefect of Anqing Prefecture; before departing he was transferred to prefect of Chizhou, and subsequently made concurrent intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in Jiang East.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed prefect of Anqing; before taking up the post he was transferred to Chizhou and made concurrent Jiang East intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 彌遠訪將材於葵，葵以範對。

translations.literal: Miyuan sought generals' talent from Kui; Kui answered with Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan asked Kui to recommend military talent; Kui named Fan.

sentences.zh: 進範直敷文閣、淮東提點刑獄兼知滁州。

translations.literal: Fan was advanced to direct attache of the Fuwén Pavilion, Huai East intendant of judicial inspection, and concurrent prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was promoted to direct attache of the Fuwén Pavilion, Huai East intendant of judicial inspection, and concurrent prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 範曰：“弟而薦 兄，不順。”

translations.literal: Fan said: "For a younger brother to recommend an elder brother is not proper."
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "For a younger brother to recommend his elder brother is improper."

sentences.zh: 以母老辭。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He declined on grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: He declined on grounds that his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 乃上書彌遠曰：“淮東之事，日異日新。

translations.literal: He then wrote to Miyuan, saying: "Affairs in Huai East change day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Miyuan: "Affairs in Huai East change by the day.

sentences.zh: 然有淮則有江，無淮則長江以北，港汊蘆葦之處，敵人皆可潛師以濟，江麵數千里，何從而防 哉。

translations.literal: Yet with the Huai there is the Yangzi; without the Huai, north of the Long River at every harbor, creek, and reed marsh the enemy can secretly move troops across— the river face stretches thousands of li; how can it be defended?
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai the Yangzi holds; without the Huai, the enemy can cross anywhere north of the Yangzi—every inlet, creek, and reed marsh offers a hidden crossing. The river front stretches thousands of li—how can it be defended?

sentences.zh: 今或謂巽辭厚惠可以啖賊，而不知陷彼款兵之計。

translations.literal: Now some say soft words and generous favors can feed the bandits, not knowing this falls into their plan to keep our troops at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Some say soft words and generous favors can appease the rebels, not seeing that this plays into their plan to lull our troops.

sentences.zh: 或謂斂兵退屯可以緩賊，而不知成彼深入之謀。

translations.literal: Some say gathering troops and withdrawing garrisons can ease the bandits, not knowing this completes their plan for deep penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Some say withdrawing garrisons can ease the rebels, not seeing that this enables their plan for deep penetration.

sentences.zh: 或欲行清野以嬰城，或欲聚烏合而浪戰，或以賊詞之乍順乍逆 而為喜懼，或以賊兵之乍進乍退而為寬緊，皆失策也。

translations.literal: Some wish to carry out scorched earth and hold the walls; some wish to gather motley crowds and fight recklessly; some feel joy or fear according to the bandits' words turning now compliant, now defiant; some feel ease or urgency according to the bandits' troops advancing and retreating by turns—all are losing strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Some want scorched earth and walled defense; others want to gather rabble and fight recklessly; some rejoice or fear as rebel words shift between compliance and defiance; others relax or panic as rebel troops advance and retreat—all are losing strategies.

sentences.zh: 失策則失淮，失淮則失江，而其失有不可勝諱者矣。

translations.literal: Lose the strategy and you lose the Huai; lose the Huai and you lose the Yangzi—and the losses will be beyond all concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Lose the strategy and you lose the Huai; lose the Huai and you lose the Yangzi—and the losses will be beyond hiding.

sentences.zh: 夫有遏寇之兵，有遊擊之兵，有討賊之兵。

translations.literal: There are troops to check invaders, troops for mobile warfare, and troops to punish bandits.
translations.idiomatic: There are blocking forces, mobile forces, and punitive forces.

sentences.zh: 今寶應之逼山 陽，天長之逼盱眙，須各增戍兵萬人，遣良將統之，賊來則堅壁以挫其鋒，不來則耀武以壓其境；

translations.literal: Now Baoying presses on Shanyang and Tianchang presses on Xuyi—each needs ten thousand additional garrison troops and a good general to command them; when bandits come, hold the walls firmly to blunt their edge; when they do not come, display force to press their territory;
translations.idiomatic: Baoying now presses Shanyang and Tianchang presses Xuyi—each needs ten thousand more garrison troops under capable generals. When rebels come, hold the walls and blunt their attack; when they do not, display force to pressure their territory;

sentences.zh: 而又觀釁伺隙，時遣偏師掩其不備，以示敢戰，使雖欲深入而畏吾 之搗其虛，此遏寇之兵也。

translations.literal: and moreover watch for openings and seize gaps, at times sending detached columns to strike where they are unprepared, to show readiness to fight, so that even if they wish to penetrate deeply they will fear our striking their weak points—this is the army that checks invaders.
translations.idiomatic: watch for openings and send detachments to strike where they are unprepared, showing readiness to fight so that even if they wish to penetrate deeply they will fear raids on their rear—this is the blocking force.

sentences.zh: 盱眙之寇，素無儲蓄，金人亦無以養之，不過分兵擄掠而食；

translations.literal: The bandits at Xuyi have no stores by nature; the Jin also have no means to sustain them—they can only divide troops to plunder for food;
translations.idiomatic: The Xuyi rebels have no stores; the Jin cannot sustain them—they can only send detachments to plunder for food;

sentences.zh: 當量出精兵，授以勇校，募土豪，出奇設伏以剿殺之，此遊擊之兵也。

translations.literal: we should deploy elite troops in measured numbers, give them brave officers, recruit local strongmen, and use surprise ambushes to hunt and kill them—this is the mobile army.
translations.idiomatic: deploy elite troops under brave officers, recruit local strongmen, and use ambushes to hunt and kill them—this is the mobile force.

sentences.zh: 惟 揚、金陵、合肥，各聚二三萬人，人物必精，將校必勇，器械必利，教閱必熟，紀律必嚴，賞罰必公，其心術念慮必人人思親其上而死其長；

translations.literal: Only at Yangzhou, Jinling, and Hefei should each gather twenty or thirty thousand men—personnel must be elite, officers brave, weapons sharp, drilling thorough, discipline strict, rewards and punishments fair, and in heart and thought every man must think to love his commander above and die for his leader;
translations.idiomatic: Only at Yangzhou, Jinling, and Hefei should we gather twenty or thirty thousand men each—elite troops, brave officers, sharp weapons, thorough drilling, strict discipline, fair rewards and punishments, and every man resolved to love his commander and die for his leader;

sentences.zh: 信能行此，半年而可以 強國，一年而可討賊矣。

translations.literal: If this can truly be carried out, in half a year the state can be strengthened; in one year bandits can be punished.
translations.idiomatic: If this is truly done, in half a year the state will be strengthened; in one year the rebels can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 賊既不能深入，擄掠復無所獲，而又懷見討之恐，則必反而求贍於金；

translations.literal: If the bandits can neither penetrate deeply nor gain anything from plunder, and again harbor fear of being punished, they will surely turn back to seek sustenance from the Jin;
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels cannot penetrate deeply, gain nothing from plunder, and live in fear of punishment, they will turn back to seek support from the Jin;

sentences.zh: 金無餘力及此，則必怨之怒之，吾於是可以嫁禍於金人矣。

translations.literal: When the Jin have no surplus strength for this, they will surely resent and rage at them—and then we can shift disaster onto the Jin people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin lack the strength to support them, they will resent and rage at the rebels—and then we can shift the blame onto the Jin.

sentences.zh: 或謂揚州 不可屯重兵，恐連賊禍，是不然。

translations.literal: Some say Yangzhou must not station heavy troops, fearing it will link disaster with the bandits—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Yangzhou must not hold heavy garrisons, fearing it will draw rebel disaster upon us—this is wrong.

sentences.zh: 揚州者，國之北門，一以統淮，一以蔽江，一以守運河，豈可無備哉。

translations.literal: Yangzhou is the state's northern gate—one part to command the Huai, one to shield the Yangzi, one to guard the Grand Canal—how can it be without defense?
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou is the realm's northern gate—commanding the Huai, shielding the Yangzi, guarding the Grand Canal—how can it go undefended?

sentences.zh: 善守者，敵不知所攻。

translations.literal: A skilled defender leaves the enemy unsure where to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled defense leaves the enemy unsure where to strike.

sentences.zh: 今若設寶應、天長二屯以扼其衝，復 重二三帥閫以張吾勢，賊將不知所攻，而敢犯我揚州哉？

translations.literal: If we now establish garrisons at Baoying and Tianchang to choke their advance, and again assign two or three heavy commanders to display our strength, the bandits will not know where to attack—how would they dare violate our Yangzhou?
translations.idiomatic: If we now garrison Baoying and Tianchang to choke their advance and assign two or three senior commanders to display our strength, the rebels will not know where to strike—how would they dare attack Yangzhou?

sentences.zh: 設使賊不知兵勢而犯揚州，是送死矣。”

translations.literal: If the bandits, ignorant of our dispositions, should attack Yangzhou, they would be delivering themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels, ignorant of our strength, attack Yangzhou, they will be marching to their deaths."

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃召範稟議，復令知池州。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The court then summoned Fan to report and deliberate, and again ordered him to serve as prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court then summoned Fan for consultation and again appointed him prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，試將作 監、知鎮江府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he served as acting director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228) he served as acting director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁母憂，求解官，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year he mourned his mother's death, requested release from office, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after his mother's death, he requested release from office; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 起復直徽猷閣、淮東安撫副使。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning as direct attache of the Huiyou Pavilion and deputy Huai East pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning as direct attache of the Huiyou Pavilion and deputy Huai East pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋轉右文殿修撰，賜章服金帶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to compiler at the Hall of Right Culture and granted golden belt and formal robes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to compiler at the Hall of Right Culture and granted golden belt and formal robes.

sentences.zh: 不得已，卒哭復視事。

translations.literal: With no choice, after the end-of-mourning rites he resumed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: With no choice, after the end-of-mourning rites he resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 又為書告廟堂：“請罷調停之 議，一請檄沿江製置司，調王明本軍駐泰興港以扼泰州下江之捷徑；

translations.literal: He again wrote to inform the court: "I request that the mediation plan be abandoned. First, order the riverine pacification commission to move Wang Ming's main force to Taixing Harbor to block the shortcut downstream from Taizhou on the Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: He again wrote to the court: "I request that mediation be abandoned. First, order the riverine pacification commission to move Wang Ming's main force to Taixing Harbor to block the shortcut downstream from Taizhou on the Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 一請檄射陽湖人為兵，屯其半高郵以製賊後，屯其半瓜州以扼賊前；

translations.literal: second, order the people of Sheyang Lake drafted as soldiers, station half at Gaoyou to check the bandits' rear, and half at Guazhou to block them in front;
translations.idiomatic: second, draft the people of Sheyang Lake as soldiers, station half at Gaoyou to check the rebels' rear and half at Guazhou to block them in front;

sentences.zh: 一請速調淮西兵合滁陽、六 合諸軍圖救江麵。

translations.literal: third, request urgent transfer of Huai West troops to combine with the Chuyang, Liuhe, and other armies to rescue the river front.
translations.idiomatic: third, urgently transfer Huai West troops to combine with the Chuyang, Liuhe, and other armies to save the river front.

sentences.zh: 不然，範雖死江皋無益也。”

translations.literal: Otherwise, though Fan should die on the riverbank, it would be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, even if Fan dies on the riverbank, it will be of no use."

sentences.zh: 朝旨乃許範刺射陽湖兵毋過二萬人，就聽節製。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The court then permitted Fan to draft Sheyang Lake troops not exceeding twenty thousand men, subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The court then permitted Fan to draft no more than twenty thousand troops from Sheyang Lake, subject to his command.

sentences.zh: 範又遺善湘書，曰：“今日與宗社同休戚者，在內惟丞 相，在外惟製使與範及範弟葵耳。

translations.literal: Fan wrote again to Shanxiang, saying: "Today those who share weal and woe with the altars of land and grain—in the capital only the chief councilor, abroad only the commissioner, Fan, and Fan's younger brother Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Fan wrote again to Shanxiang: "Today those who share weal and woe with the altars of state—in the capital only the chief councilor, abroad only the commissioner, Fan, and Fan's younger brother Kui.

sentences.zh: 賊若得誌，此四家必無存理。”

translations.literal: If the bandits achieve their aim, these four households can certainly have no hope of survival.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels succeed, these four households will surely have no hope of survival."

sentences.zh: 於是討賊之謀遂決，遂戮全。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Thereupon the plan to punish the bandits was settled, and Quan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the plan to destroy the rebels was settled, and Quan was executed.

sentences.zh: 進範兵部侍郎、淮東安撫使兼知揚州兼江淮製置司參謀官，以次復淮 東。

translations.literal: Fan was promoted to vice-minister of War, Huai East pacification commissioner and concurrent prefect of Yangzhou and planning officer of the Jiang-Huai Pacification Commission; in sequence Huai East was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was promoted to vice-minister of War, Huai East pacification commissioner and concurrent prefect of Yangzhou and planning officer on the Jiang-Huai Pacification Commission; step by step Huai East was recovered.

sentences.zh: 加吏部侍郎，進工部尚書、沿江製置副使，權移司兼知黃州，尋兼淮西製置副使。

translations.literal: He was further made vice-minister of Personnel, then vice-minister of Works and deputy riverine pacification commissioner, with headquarters temporarily moved and concurrent prefect of Huangzhou; soon also deputy Huai West pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made vice-minister of Personnel, then vice-minister of Works and deputy riverine pacification commissioner, with headquarters temporarily moved and concurrent prefect of Huangzhou; soon he also served as deputy Huai West pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為兩淮製置使、節製巡邊軍馬，仍兼沿江製置副使。

translations.literal: Before long he became dual-Huai pacification commissioner, with authority to command frontier patrol forces, still concurrently deputy riverine pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became dual-Huai pacification commissioner with authority over frontier patrol forces, still concurrently deputy riverine pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又進 端明殿學士，京河關陝宣撫使、知開封府、東京留守兼江、淮製置使。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall, commissioner of the Jinghe-Guanxi Pacification Commission, prefect of Kaifeng, Eastern Capital regent, and concurrent Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner.
