translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall, Jinghe-Guanxi pacification commissioner, prefect of Kaifeng, Eastern Capital regent, and concurrent Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入洛之師大潰，乃授京湖安撫製置使兼知襄陽府。

translations.literal: When the army entering Luoyang routed in great disorder, he was appointed Jing-Hu pacification commissioner and concurrent prefect of Xiangyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the army sent into Luoyang routed in disaster, he was appointed Jing-Hu pacification commissioner and concurrent prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 範至，則倚王旻、樊文彬、李伯淵、黃國弼 數人為腹心，朝夕酣狎，了無上下之序。

translations.literal: When Fan arrived, he relied on Wang Min, Fan Wenbin, Li Boyuan, Huang Guobi, and several others as his inner circle, carousing together day and night with no sense of rank between superior and subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan arrived, he relied on Wang Min, Fan Wenbin, Li Boyuan, Huang Guobi, and several others as his inner circle, carousing day and night with no regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 民訟邊防，一切廢馳。

translations.literal: Lawsuits and border defense were entirely neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits and border defense were entirely neglected.

sentences.zh: 屬南北軍將交爭，範失於撫禦。

translations.literal: When northern and southern army officers came into conflict, Fan failed in pacification and control.
translations.idiomatic: When northern and southern army officers clashed, Fan failed to pacify and control them.

sentences.zh: 於是北軍王旻內叛，李伯淵繼之，焚襄陽北去；

translations.literal: Thereupon the northern army officer Wang Min rebelled from within, Li Boyuan followed suit, and they burned Xiangyang and fled north;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the northern army officer Wang Min rebelled from within, Li Boyuan followed, and they burned Xiangyang and fled north;

sentences.zh: 南軍大將李虎不救 焚，不定變，乃因之劫掠。

translations.literal: the southern army great general Li Hu did not rescue from the fires, failed to quell the disturbance, and took the opportunity to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: the southern army great general Li Hu did not fight the fires, failed to quell the disturbance, and took the opportunity to plunder.

sentences.zh: 城中官民尚四萬七千有奇，錢糧在倉庫者無慮三十萬，弓矢器械二十有四庫，皆為敵有。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners remaining in the city still numbered more than forty-seven thousand; grain and money in the warehouses amounted to no less than three hundred thousand, with bows, arrows, and weapons in twenty-four storehouses—all fell to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners still in the city numbered more than forty-seven thousand; grain and money in the warehouses came to no less than three hundred thousand, with bows, arrows, and weapons in twenty-four storehouses—all fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 蓋自岳飛收復百三十年，生聚繁庶，城高池深， 甲於西陲，一旦灰燼，禍至慘也。

translations.literal: For one hundred thirty years since Yue Fei recovered it, the place had grown populous and prosperous, with high walls and deep moats, foremost in the western frontier—yet in a single day it became ash, a disaster of appalling severity.
translations.idiomatic: For one hundred thirty years since Yue Fei recovered it, the city had grown populous and prosperous, with high walls and deep moats, foremost on the western frontier—yet in a single day it was ash; the disaster was appalling.

sentences.zh: 言者劾範，降三官落職，依舊制置使。

translations.literal: Memorialists impeached Fan; he was demoted three ranks and stripped of office, remaining only as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists impeached Fan; he was demoted three ranks and stripped of office, retaining only his pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 尋奉祠，以言罷；

translations.literal: Soon he received a temple stipend and was dismissed on account of criticism;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received a temple stipend and was dismissed on account of criticism;

sentences.zh: 論者未已，再降兩官，送建寧府居住。

translations.literal: critics not satisfied, he was demoted two more ranks and sent to reside at Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: critics still unsatisfied, he was demoted two more ranks and sent to reside at Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，敘復官職，與宮觀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi his offices were restored by seniority and he was given a Taoist abbey post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaxi (1239) his offices were restored by seniority and he was given a Taoist abbey post.

sentences.zh: 四 年，知靜江府，後卒於家。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture and later died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Jingjiang and later died at home.

sentences.zh: 謝方叔，字德方，威州人。

translations.literal: Xie Fangshu, courtesy name Defang, was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangshu, styled Defang, was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年進士，曆官監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Jiading and successively served as surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the sixteenth year of Jiading (1223) and served successively as surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：“秉剛德以回上帝之心，奮威斷以回天下之勢，或者猶 恐前習便嬖之人，有以私陛下之聽而悅陛下之心，則前日之畏者怠，憂者喜，慮者玩矣。

translations.literal: In a memorial he submitted: "Uphold firm virtue to turn back Heaven's heart; rouse authoritative resolve to turn back the realm's momentum—or perhaps one still fears that those accustomed to flattery from before will privately sway Your Majesty's ear and delight Your Majesty's heart, and then those who were fearful will grow lax, those who were worried will rejoice, and those who were cautious will grow careless.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he submitted: "Uphold firm virtue to turn Heaven's heart; rouse decisive authority to turn the realm's momentum—or perhaps one still fears that those accustomed to flattery will privately sway Your Majesty's ear and delight your heart, so that those who were fearful grow lax, those who were worried rejoice, and those who were cautious grow careless.

sentences.zh: 左右前後之人，進憂危恐懼之言者，是納忠於上也；

translations.literal: Of those around and before Your Majesty, those who offer words of peril, fear, and dread are offering loyalty to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Of those around and before Your Majesty, those who speak of peril, fear, and dread are loyal to the throne;

sentences.zh: 進燕安逸樂之言者，是 不忠於上也。

translations.literal: those who offer words of ease, comfort, and pleasure are disloyal to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: those who speak of ease, comfort, and pleasure are disloyal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡有水旱盜賊之奏者，必忠臣也；

translations.literal: Whenever there are memorials on flood, drought, or banditry, the submitter must be a loyal minister;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there are memorials on flood, drought, or banditry, the submitter must be a loyal minister;

sentences.zh: 有諂諛蒙蔽之言者，必佞臣也。

translations.literal: whenever there are words of flattery, deception, and concealment, the speaker must be a sycophant.
translations.idiomatic: whenever there are words of flattery, deception, and concealment, the speaker must be a sycophant.

sentences.zh: 陛下享玉食珍羞之奉，當思兩淮流莩轉壑之可矜；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty enjoys jade dishes and rare delicacies, you should think of the pitiable refugees of the two Huai, wandering corpses filling the ditches;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty enjoys jade dishes and rare delicacies, you should think of the pitiable refugees of the two Huai, corpses filling the ditches;

sentences.zh: 聞管弦鍾鼓之聲，當思西蜀白骨如 山之可念。”

translations.literal: when you hear strings, pipes, bells, and drums, you should think of the white bones of western Shu piled like mountains, worthy of remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: when you hear strings, pipes, bells, and drums, you should think of the white bones of western Shu piled like mountains."

sentences.zh: 又言：“崇儉德以契天理，儲人才以供天職，恢遠略以需天討，行仁政以答天意。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He also said: "Honor frugal virtue to accord with Heaven's principle, store talent to supply Heaven's offices, restore far-reaching strategy to await Heaven's punishment, and practice benevolent government to answer Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Honor frugal virtue to accord with Heaven's principle, store talent for Heaven's offices, restore far-reaching strategy to await Heaven's punishment, and practice benevolent government to answer Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 差知衡州，除宗正少卿，又除太常少卿兼國史編修、實錄檢 討。

translations.literal: He was assigned to Hengzhou, appointed vice-director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, then vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent appointment as national history compiler and veritable records examiner.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to Hengzhou, appointed vice-director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, then vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent appointment as national history compiler and veritable records examiner.

sentences.zh: 時劉漢弼、杜範、徐元傑相繼死，方叔言：“元傑之死，陛下既為命官鞫獄，立賞捕奸，罪人未得，忠冤未伸。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Hanbi, Du Fan, and Xu Yuanjie died in succession. Fangshu said: "In Yuanjie's death, Your Majesty has already ordered officials to investigate, set rewards to capture the villains—the guilty have not been found and loyal innocence has not been vindicated.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Hanbi, Du Fan, and Xu Yuanjie died in succession. Fangshu said: "In Yuanjie's death, Your Majesty has already ordered officials to investigate and set rewards to capture the villains—yet the guilty have not been found and loyal innocence has not been vindicated.

sentences.zh: 陛下苟不始終主持，將恐紀綱掃 地，而國無以為國矣。”

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not hold fast from beginning to end, I fear the pillars of government will be swept clean and the state will have nothing by which to be a state.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not see this through from beginning to end, I fear the pillars of government will be swept away and the state will cease to be a state."

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，進對，言：“操存本於方寸，治亂係於天下。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He was transferred to palace censor, and in an audience said: "Self-mastery lies in the heart's inch; order and disorder depend on the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to palace censor, and in an audience said: "Self-mastery lies in the heart; order and disorder depend on the realm.

sentences.zh: 人主宅如法宮蠖之邃，朝夕親近者左右近習承意伺旨之徒，往往覘上之所好， 不過保恩寵、希貨利而已。

translations.literal: The ruler dwells deep as in a silkworm chamber; those close at hand morning and evening—the attendants and favorites who read his will—often watch what the sovereign likes, seeking nothing beyond preserving favor and hoping for goods and profit.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler dwells deep as in a silkworm chamber; those close at hand morning and evening—the attendants and favorites who read his will—often watch what the sovereign likes, seeking nothing beyond preserving favor and profit.

sentences.zh: 而冥冥之中，或有遊揚之說，潛伏而莫之覺。

translations.literal: Yet in the hidden depths there may be roaming persuasions, lurking unnoticed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the hidden depths there may be roaming persuasions, lurking unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 防微杜漸，實以是心主之。”

translations.literal: To guard against the subtle and stop the gradual—this truly depends on the heart's mastery.
translations.idiomatic: To guard against the subtle and stop the gradual—this truly depends on the heart's mastery."

sentences.zh: 又言：“今日為兩淮謀者有五：一曰明間諜，二曰修馬政，三 曰營山水砦，四曰經理近城之方田，五曰加重遏絕遊騎及救奪擄掠之賞罰。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He also said: "Today those who plan for the two Huai have five points: first, clarify espionage; second, restore horse administration; third, build mountain-and-water stockades; fourth, manage the square fields near the cities; fifth, increase rewards and punishments for blocking roaming cavalry and rescuing captives."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Today those who plan for the two Huai have five points: first, clarify espionage; second, restore horse administration; third, build mountain-and-water stockades; fourth, manage the square fields near the cities; fifth, increase rewards and punishments for blocking roaming cavalry and rescuing captives."

sentences.zh: 請行限田，請錄朱熹門人胡安定、呂燾、蔡模，詔皆從之。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) He requested implementation of land limits and requested recording of Zhu Xi's disciples Hu Anding, Lü Yan, and Cai Mo; the edicts all granted these.
translations.idiomatic: He requested implementation of land limits and requested recording of Zhu Xi's disciples Hu Anding, Lü Yan, and Cai Mo; the edicts all granted these.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎兼權給事中，升兼侍講，正授刑部侍郎，權國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: Acting vice-minister of Punishments and acting drafter; promoted to concurrent lecturer-in-waiting; formally appointed vice-minister of Punishments with acting appointment as national history compiler and veritable records examiner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice-minister of Punishments and acting drafter, was promoted to concurrent lecturer-in-waiting, was formally appointed vice-minister of Punishments with acting appointment as national history compiler and veritable records examiner.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 淳祐九年，拜參知政事，封永康郡侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chunyou he was appointed participant in governance and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chunyou (1249) he was appointed participant in governance and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一年，特授知樞密院事兼參知政事，尋拜左丞相兼樞密使，進封惠國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was specially appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and participant in governance; soon he was appointed left chief councilor and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Duke of Huiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was specially appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and participant in governance; soon he was appointed left chief councilor and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Duke of Huiguo.

sentences.zh: 勸帝以愛身育德。

translations.literal: He urged the Emperor to cherish his person and cultivate virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the Emperor to cherish his person and cultivate virtue.

sentences.zh: 屬監察御史洪天錫論宦者盧允升、董宋臣，疏留中不下，大宗正寺丞趙崇璠移書方叔云：“閹寺驕恣特甚，宰執不聞正救，台諫不敢誰何，一新入孤立之察官，乃 銳意出身攻之，此豈易得哉？

translations.literal: When surveillance censor Hong Tiansi memorialized against eunuchs Lu Yunshang and Dong Songchen, the memorial was retained without action. Grand Imperial Clan Court registrar Zhao Chongli wrote to Fangshu, saying: "The palace eunuchs are insolent beyond measure; the chief ministers offer no upright rescue, the censors and remonstrators dare not challenge them, and a newly appointed isolated censor is boldly risking himself to attack them—is this easily come by?
translations.idiomatic: When surveillance censor Hong Tiansi memorialized against eunuchs Lu Yunshang and Dong Songchen, the memorial was retained without action. Grand Imperial Clan Court registrar Zhao Chongli wrote to Fangshu: "The palace eunuchs are insolent beyond measure; the chief ministers offer no upright rescue, the censors and remonstrators dare not challenge them, and a newly appointed isolated censor is boldly risking himself to attack them—is this easily come by?

sentences.zh: 側耳數日，寂無所聞，公議不責備他人，而責備於宰相。

translations.literal: For days on end one listens and hears nothing—public opinion does not blame others but blames the chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: For days on end one listens and hears nothing—public opinion does not blame others but blames the chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 不然，倉卒出御筆，某人授少卿，亦必無可遏之理矣，丞相不可謂非我責也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, if the Emperor should suddenly issue a brush edict appointing someone vice minister, there would certainly be no stopping it—the chief councilor cannot say this is not his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if the Emperor should suddenly issue a brush edict appointing someone vice minister, there would be no stopping it—the chief councilor cannot say this is not his responsibility.

sentences.zh: 丞相得君最深，名位已極。

translations.literal: The chief councilor enjoys the deepest favor of the sovereign and has reached the summit of rank.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor enjoys the deepest favor of the sovereign and has reached the summit of rank.

sentences.zh: 倘言之勝，宗社賴之；

translations.literal: If your words prevail, the altars of state will rely on you;
translations.idiomatic: If your words prevail, the altars of state will rely on you;

sentences.zh: 言之不勝，則去。

translations.literal: if they do not prevail, then resign.
translations.idiomatic: if they do not prevail, then resign.

sentences.zh: 去則諸君必不容不爭，是勝亦勝，負亦勝，況未必去耶。”

translations.literal: If you resign, the others will surely not fail to contest—a victory either way, defeat is also victory, and you may not resign at all.
translations.idiomatic: If you resign, the others will surely not fail to contest—win or lose, you win either way, and you may not resign at all."

sentences.zh: 方叔得書，有赧色。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Fangshu received the letter and showed embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshu received the letter and showed embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 翼 日，果得御筆授天錫大理少卿，而天錫去國。

translations.literal: The next day an imperial brush edict indeed appointed Tiansi vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and Tiansi left the court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an imperial brush edict indeed appointed Tiansi vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and Tiansi left the court.

sentences.zh: 於是太學生池元堅、太常寺丞趙崇潔、左史李昴英皆論擊允升、宋臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the student of the Imperial Academy Chi Yuanjian, Court of Imperial Sacrifices registrar Zhao Chongjie, and left recorder Li Angying all criticized Yunshang and Songchen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Imperial Academy student Chi Yuanjian, Court of Imperial Sacrifices registrar Zhao Chongjie, and left recorder Li Angying all criticized Yunshang and Songchen.

sentences.zh: 而讒者又曰：“天錫之論，方叔意也。”

translations.literal: But slanderers also said: "Tiansi's memorial was Fangshu's idea."
translations.idiomatic: But slanderers also said: "Tiansi's memorial was Fangshu's idea."

sentences.zh: 及天錫 之去，亦曰：“方叔意也。”

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) And when Tiansi left, they also said: "It was Fangshu's idea."
translations.idiomatic: And when Tiansi left, they also said: "It was Fangshu's idea."

sentences.zh: 方叔上疏自解，於是監察御史朱應元論方叔，罷相。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) Fangshu submitted a memorial in self-defense; thereupon surveillance censor Zhu Yingyuan memorialized against Fangshu and he was dismissed as chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshu submitted a memorial in self-defense; thereupon surveillance censor Zhu Yingyuan memorialized against Fangshu and he was dismissed as chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 既罷，允升、宋臣猶以為未快，厚賂太學生林自養，上書力詆天錫、方叔，且 曰：“乞誅方叔，使天下明知宰相台諫之去，出自獨斷，於內侍初無預焉。”

translations.literal: After dismissal, Yunshang and Songchen still thought it insufficient; they bribed student of the Imperial Academy Lin Ziyang to submit a memorial vigorously denouncing Tiansi and Fangshu, further saying: "I beg that Fangshu be executed so the realm may clearly know that the departure of chief councilor and censor originated in the sovereign's independent decision and had no connection with the inner attendants at all."
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal, Yunshang and Songchen still thought it insufficient; they bribed Imperial Academy student Lin Ziyang to submit a memorial vigorously denouncing Tiansi and Fangshu, further saying: "I beg that Fangshu be executed so the realm may clearly know that the departure of chief councilor and censor originated in the sovereign's independent decision and had no connection with the inner attendants at all."

sentences.zh: 書既上，學舍惡自養黨奸，相與鳴鼓攻之，上書以聲其罪。

translations.literal: (close quotation mark) After the memorial was submitted, the student quarters detested Lin Ziyang as a partisan of villains and together beat drums to attack him, submitting memorials to proclaim his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, the student quarters detested Lin Ziyang as a partisan of villains and together beat drums to attack him, submitting memorials to proclaim his crimes.

sentences.zh: 乃授方叔觀文殿大學士、提 舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Fangshu was then appointed grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshu was then appointed grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 復以監察御史李衢兩劾，褫職罷祠。

translations.literal: Again impeached twice by surveillance censor Li Qu, his office was stripped and his abbey post revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Again impeached twice by surveillance censor Li Qu, his office was stripped and his abbey post revoked.

sentences.zh: 後依舊職，與祠，起居郎召澤、中書舍人林存劾罷；

translations.literal: Later his former offices were restored and he was given an abbey post; but when attendant gentleman Zhao Ze and drafting official Lin Cun memorialized for his dismissal, he was removed;
translations.idiomatic: Later his former offices were restored and he was given an abbey post; but when attendant gentleman Zhao Ze and drafting official Lin Cun memorialized for his dismissal, he was removed;

sentences.zh: 監察御史章士元請更與降削，竄廣南。

translations.literal: surveillance censor Zhang Shiyuan requested further demotion and banishment to the far south.
translations.idiomatic: surveillance censor Zhang Shiyuan requested further demotion and banishment to the far south.

sentences.zh: 景定二年，請致仕，乃敘 復官職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingding he requested retirement; his offices were then restored by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingding (1261) he requested retirement; his offices were then restored by seniority.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，方叔以一琴、一鶴、金丹一粒來進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong ascended the throne, Fangshu came to present a zither, a crane, and one golden pill.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Duzong ascended the throne, Fangshu came to present a zither, a crane, and one golden elixir pill.

sentences.zh: 丞相賈似道恐其希望，諷權右司郎官盧越、左司諫趙順孫、給事中馮夢得、右正言黃鏞相繼請奪方叔官職封爵，製置使呂文德願以己官贖其罪。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Jia Sidao, fearing he sought favor, insinuated to the right director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Yue, left remonstrating officer Zhao Shunsun, drafter Feng Mengde, and right rectifier Huang Yong in succession to request stripping Fangshu's offices and titles; pacification commissioner Lü Wende offered his own office to redeem Fangshu's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Jia Sidao, fearing he sought favor, insinuated to the right director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Yue, left remonstrating officer Zhao Shunsun, drafter Feng Mengde, and right rectifier Huang Yong in succession to request stripping Fangshu's offices and titles; pacification commissioner Lü Wende offered his own office to redeem Fangshu's guilt.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳七年，詔敘復致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianchun an edict restored his retirement status.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianchun (1271) an edict restored his retirement status.

sentences.zh: 八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died.

sentences.zh: 特贈少師，方叔在相位，子弟幹政，若讒餘玠之類是也。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor. While Fangshu was chief councilor, his sons and younger brothers interfered in government affairs—slandering Yu Jie was an example of this.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Preceptor. While Fangshu was chief councilor, his sons and younger brothers interfered in government affairs—slandering Yu Jie was one example.

sentences.zh: 論曰：喬行簡弘深好賢，論事通諫。

translations.literal: The discourse says: Qiao Xingjian was broad-minded and profound, fond of the worthy; in discussing affairs he communicated remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Qiao Xingjian was magnanimous and profound, fond of talent; in counsel he spoke with forthright remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 範鍾、遊似同在相位，皆謹飭自將，而意見不侔。

translations.literal: Fan Zhong and You Si were both in the chief councilor's post, each strict and self-restrained, yet their views did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhong and You Si both held the chief councilor's post, each strict and self-restrained, yet their views did not agree.

sentences.zh: 趙方預計二子後當若何，而葵、範所立，皆如所言，所謂知子莫若父也。

translations.literal: Zhao Fang foresaw how his two sons would fare afterward, and what Kui and Fan achieved matched what he said—the proverb says no one knows a son like his father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fang foresaw how his two sons would fare, and what Kui and Fan achieved matched what he said—as the proverb has it, no one knows a son like his father.

sentences.zh: 然 宋自端平以來，捍禦淮、蜀兩邊者，非葵材館之士，即其偏裨之將。

translations.literal: Yet since the Duanping era, those who defended the Huai and Shu frontiers were none other than Kui and his staff officers, or his subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the Duanping era, those who defended the Huai and Shu frontiers were none other than Kui and his staff officers, or his subordinate generals.

sentences.zh: 朝廷倚之，如長城之勢。

translations.literal: The court relied on them like the strength of the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The court relied on them like the Great Wall itself.

sentences.zh: 及其筋力既老，而衛國之誌不衰，亦曰壯哉！

translations.literal: When their strength was already aged, yet their resolve to guard the state did not decline—one must also say, how vigorous!
translations.idiomatic: When their strength was already spent, yet their resolve to guard the state did not fade—one must also say, how vigorous!

sentences.zh: 謝方叔相業無過人者，晚 困於權臣，至以玩好丹劑為人主壽，坐是貶削，有愧金鏡多矣！

translations.literal: Xie Fangshu's ministerial achievements were nothing extraordinary; in his late years he was trapped by powerful ministers, even offering curios and elixirs to prolong the sovereign's life—for this he suffered demotion, falling far short of the golden mirror indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangshu's ministerial achievements were nothing extraordinary; in his late years he was trapped by powerful ministers, even offering curios and elixirs to prolong the sovereign's life—for this he suffered demotion, falling far short of the golden mirror indeed!
